notes: value_si is hydrogen. He 24.587 eV and H2 15.43 eV sit in the same tens-of-eV class. Pair production is rest-mass creation and must not be folded into I.

observed_text: If the atom is already stripped of that electron, that particular gate is gone; a deeper gate may remain.
implied_text: Missing hardware closes that named ionization step. Multi-electron atoms are a ladder of gates, not one reusable cliff.
description: An already-empty valence slot cannot open I of that charge state.
value_text: electron already stripped; deeper I may remain
notes: Inner-shell rungs are filed as x-ray-absorption-edge.

observed_text: Below I this conversion does not occur. A cold atomic hydrogen cell does not conduct. At room temperature kT ≈ 0.026 eV, so I/kT ~ 500 for hydrogen: the thermal tail does not ionize a cold gas.
implied_text: Under-threshold input (hν, projectile KE, or the relevant scale of kT) is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of the effect.
description: Below I the gas stays neutral in this channel.
notes: Residual conductivity of a real gas is then impurities, cosmic-ray seeds, or other channels — not opening I.

observed_text: One atom or molecule is the hardware for one conversion. There is no collective buffer that must be filled before a single ionization can happen.
implied_text: A macroscopic ionized gas is the summed output of a large population. Density enters later as recombination, screening, and avalanches — sequels, not the gate.
description: Negative spatial-buffer spec: the gate is single-particle.
notes: Dielectric-breakdown owns the many-body field avalanche that uses this gate as a step.

observed_text: Two clocks: observation bandwidth Δf, and the thermal electromagnetic / electronic clock kT/h (≈ 6.25 THz at 300 K; tens of gigahertz at a few kelvin). The classical envelope fails when hf is no longer small compared with kT.
implied_text: Narrowing Δf is a longer average and kills the integrated variance. Drive or observation above kT/h leaves the classical Nyquist formula for the high-frequency envelope.
description: Classical 4kTR is an averaging-window statement below kT/h.
notes: h and k are defined. 6.25 THz is arithmetic, not an extracted machine clock. Ordinary audio and RF sit far below kT/h at 300 K; cryogenic microwave work does not.

observed_text: The mapping does not supply a resistor-volume cliff, and the data do not demand one. The high-frequency form is kept as an envelope; whether an hf/2 term is an available voltage on a given bench is not settled by this entry.
implied_text: Zero-point arguments about what a voltmeter can extract at T=0 are omitted. That is a recorded gap in interpretation, not a gap in the T→0 / Δf→0 collapse class.
description: No volume cliff is extracted, and zero-point voltage is not filed as a QSA output.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium.

observed_text: Classical Nyquist envelope ⟨V^2⟩ = 4kTRΔf. At 300 K a 1 kΩ resistor delivers ≈ 4.07 nV Hz^{-1/2}; a 50 Ω resistor delivers ≈ 0.91 nV Hz^{-1/2}.
implied_text: A white voltage floor 4kTR is the electrical average of the thermal population, with a definite integrated variance once Δf is stated.
description: The stable output is the Nyquist floor. It is the electrical fluctuation–dissipation twin of D = kT/γ.
notes: k is defined. The nV Hz^{-1/2} figures are arithmetic at 300 K, not extracted machine constants. Cross-cite brownian-motion.

observed_text: None holding a latched state. Sending the resistor into the superconducting state (R→0) removes the voltage noise by removing R.
implied_text: Noise is the electrical average of a dissipative element, not a stored configuration.
description: Johnson–Nyquist has no energy barrier that stores a state.
notes: Cross-cite superconductivity for the R→0 realization.

observed_text: Δf→0 → integrated variance → 0. A measurement taken in a vanishing bandwidth is quiet. The spectral density may still be 4kTR; the reading of a zero-width filter is not a noise power.
implied_text: Lengthen the average until the variance is gone. That is the family clock failure run on the filter.
description: Vanishing bandwidth collapses the integrated Nyquist variance.

observed_text: R→0 → voltage noise → 0 (a short). A superconductor below T_c is the clean material realization of that limit. R→∞ (open) collapses current noise instead.
implied_text: Remove the dissipative resource and the voltage floor collapses.
description: A short, including a superconductor, has no Johnson voltage noise.
notes: Cross-cite superconductivity. Skin effect retunes the R(f) that Nyquist consumes; it does not replace Nyquist.

observed_text: T→0 → ⟨V^2⟩→0 in the Nyquist formula. Cooling the resistor toward T=0 kills the classical noise.
implied_text: Shrink the thermal resource and the electrical average vanishes.
description: Classical Johnson noise collapses as T→0.
notes: Shares this collapse with brownian-motion (D = kT/γ). Zero-point bookkeeping at T=0 is omitted; see the consistency-gap row.

observed_text: There is no universal resistor volume at which 4kTRΔf starts working. A lithographed nanometre-scale resistor still presents the Nyquist floor once it has a well-defined R and a bath T. Extra noise in small devices is shot, telegraph, or two-level-system, not a missing thermal floor.
implied_text: The hardware is a dissipative element with stable R, coupled to a thermal population with stable T, averaged over the chosen Δf. Inventing a minimum N of carriers would be a conjecture.
description: Johnson–Nyquist names a statistical average and does not attach a resistor-volume cliff.
notes: 1/f and TLS noise sit on top of the Nyquist floor; they are a different output, not the collapse of this effect.

observed_text: Voltage-frequency lock ν = (2e/h) V ≈ 483.6 MHz/μV. Equivalently V = (h/2e) ν = Φ0 ν, with Φ0 = h/2e = 2.0678e-15 Wb.
implied_text: The AC Josephson lock is the clock: a microvolt bias oscillates at hundreds of megahertz; a millivolt bias sits in the sub-terahertz. This is a frequency locked to a voltage, not a plasma-period screening cycle.
description: The weak-link clock is 483.6 MHz per microvolt of DC bias.
notes: value_si is Hz per volt. Shapiro steps are the same clock read out against an external microwave drive.

observed_text: The measured charge increment in h/2e is taken from the voltage-frequency lock and from the flux quantum.
implied_text: QSA does not derive why the increment is 2e rather than e from node rules alone. That increment is recorded as data. No pairing story is required to locate the collapses, and none is added.
description: The 2e in h/2e is located as a measured increment, not derived from node rules.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; the open item is the origin of the increment, not the location of the collapses. RSJ C and R are descriptive bookkeeping.

observed_text: The junction oscillates at ν = (2e/h) V. An applied microwave tone produces constant-voltage Shapiro steps at Vn = n h f / 2e. The ratio is used as a voltage standard.
implied_text: The synchronized output is a universal voltage-frequency lock V = (h/2e) ν once a voltage is present, together with a dissipationless weak-link current at V=0 for |I| ≤ Ic.
description: The Josephson machine emits a metrological V–ν lock at 2e/h, and a zero-voltage supercurrent below Ic.
notes: Complementary metrological lock to quantum-hall-effect (RK = h/e²).

observed_text: Ic is set by the junction (area, barrier transparency, electrode gap) and is not a universal constant. A DC supercurrent exists only for |I| ≤ Ic.
implied_text: Ic is the current threshold that protects the zero-voltage branch. The electrode gap is the energy scale that vanishes at Tc and takes Ic with it.
description: The zero-voltage branch is gated by a junction-specific Ic, not by a universal current.
notes: A flux of order Φ0 through the junction is a field threshold that suppresses Ic without first destroying the electrodes.

observed_text: Above Ic a finite DC voltage appears across the link. For |I| > Ic the junction is on a resistive branch and V ≠ 0.
implied_text: Current over-budget ends the zero-voltage branch. The voltage-frequency lock can then run; the dissipationless DC current is gone.
description: Crossing Ic collapses the V=0 supercurrent.
notes: T > Tc in either electrode is a coarser collapse: the parent condensate is gone. Electrode Hc / Hc2 is owned by superconductivity / type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: Magnetic flux through the junction area of order Φ0 modulates Ic (Fraunhofer diffraction in a uniform rectangular junction). Φ0 = h/2e = 2.0678e-15 Wb.
implied_text: A flux of order Φ0 is a field threshold that suppresses Ic without first destroying the electrodes.
description: Junction-scale flux of one quantum collapses Ic by interference, not by driving the electrodes normal.
notes: Same Φ0 as flux-quantization; that is a consistency check, not two constants. Electrode-scale Hc2 is a different, coarser collapse.

observed_text: Thickening the barrier sends Ic to zero. A thicker continuous insulator leaves two separate superconductors.
implied_text: Spatial over-provisioning of the insulator starves the coupling resource and the weak-link current disappears.
description: A too-thick (or too-opaque) barrier is the spatial collapse of the Josephson machine.
value_text: barrier thicker than a few nm
notes: Same few-nanometre window as the hardware-scale row; this row is the starved-coupling failure.

observed_text: SIS oxide barriers that still carry a usable weak-link current are a few nanometres thick. A thicker continuous insulator drives Ic → 0; the electrodes then behave as two separate superconductors.
implied_text: Two nested buffers: each electrode must be a superconducting condensate, and they must be coupled by a weak link whose thickness sits in a narrow window. The load-bearing node of this artifact is the phase difference φ across that under-coupled spatial buffer.
description: The Josephson machine is a few-nanometre weak link between two parent condensates; thicker coupling is starved and Ic vanishes.
notes: value_si is the order of a few nanometres. Absent barrier, the two sides are one superconductor with no junction degree of freedom. Electrode Tc / ξ / gap are owned by superconductivity.

observed_text: Moments inside a wall still precess at the ≈ 28 GHz/T carrier. Pattern changes are wall-motion events whose speed is set by damping, eddy currents, and pinning, and is far below that carrier.
implied_text: A static pattern has no ongoing clock cost. Write latency of a domain pattern is wall motion, not the precession carrier.
description: Domain walls inherit the 28 GHz/T spin clock; the partition itself moves on a much slower pinning-limited clock.
notes: File quotes ≈ 28 GHz T^{-1}, not the 28.025 figure of the parent latch.

observed_text: Why one sample shows closure domains, another stripes, another a maze is a magnetostatic-plus-pinning problem. Continuum A and K are taken as measured inputs to δw and γw. Wall pinning sets technical Hc.
implied_text: QSA does not produce A and K from a more primitive buffer, and does not select the imaged pattern from node rules. The same mesoscale Hc gap reappears as pinning.
description: Pattern choice and the pinning that sets technical Hc remain mesoscale data; the wall-width and single-domain cliffs do not depend on closing them.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for this reason.

observed_text: In zero applied field the net moment can be far below saturation even though each domain is locally ordered. Net moment ranges from ≈ 0 (closed pattern) to saturation (walls expelled).
implied_text: Stable output is a static partition of the aligned population, with measured wall width ~√(A/K) and a net moment set by how closed the pattern is.
description: Domains emit a held partition, not a requirement of a large net dipole.
notes: Wall positions are imaged (Bitter, Kerr, MFM) and are static at rest.

observed_text: A static domain pattern at rest produces no continuous hysteresis heat. Wall positions are static at rest: no continuous power is required to hold a given partition.
implied_text: Hold-power of a static partition is zero. Wall motion around a hysteresis loop dissipates the loop area.
description: Holding a domain pattern costs zero watts. Energy is spent only when walls move.

observed_text: Wall energy per unit area scales as √(AK) (Bloch form γw ≈ 4√(AK)). Soft, low-K magnets have cheap, wide walls; hard magnets have expensive, narrow walls. Holding a static partition costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Each domain is the parent anisotropy latch. The wall is a distributed transition whose area cost is the price of a partition. Pinning at grains and defects is the mesoscale barrier that shows up as Hc.
description: Partition cost is wall area times √(AK); static patterns have no hold-power bill.
notes: No numerical γw is computed in the file.

observed_text: A large enough applied field drives walls out. The technical saturation field is microstructure-dependent and is not Ha. At saturation the walls are gone and the body is one domain.
implied_text: Applied H expels walls → the partition is gone. The local latch is still present.
description: Saturation is destruction of the domain pattern, not of the local directional latch.
value_text: H large enough to expel walls (≠ H_a)
notes: T > Tc removes local order and therefore domains; grain-scale KV collapse is superparamagnetism, below the domain problem.

observed_text: Single-domain critical size scales as √(AK)/(μ0 Ms²) (Kittel / Brown class). In soft 3d metals that length is tens of nanometres; in high-K magnets it is larger.
implied_text: Below the wall-vs-magnetostatic cliff the pattern never forms; the particle is one latch cell, not a partition.
description: The domain pattern dies at a material-dependent single-domain size; there is no universal millimetre-scale domain period.
value_text: tens of nm (soft 3d); larger in high-K
notes: Prefactors depend on assumed shape and wall type; the existence of a size cliff is the measured fact. A numerical critical diameter for a named particle is medium.

observed_text: Wall width scales as √(A/K) (Bloch form δw ≈ π√(A/K)). A is of order 10^{-11} J/m in Fe, Co, Ni. Fe-like cubic K1 (~10^4 J/m³) gives tens of nanometres; NdFeB-like K1 ≈ 4.5 MJ/m³ gives a few nanometres.
implied_text: The wall is a measured spatial buffer, not a mathematical point. Narrower than that and the two domains have merged.
description: A resolved domain wall is a transition strip of nanometre-to-tens-of-nanometres width set by √(A/K).
value_text: few nm (NdFeB) to tens of nm (soft Fe)
notes: value_si is the soft-Fe order of magnitude stated as tens of nanometres. A ~ 10^{-11} J m^{-1} is taken as a measured input.

observed_text: Magnetic side: precession / domain-wall clocks of the magnet entries. Mechanical side: acoustic transit of elasticity. Laboratory λ(H) loops are limited by the field sweep and by eddy currents / walls, not by the 28 GHz/T carrier.
implied_text: The length-change clock is the magnet’s write / wall motion plus acoustic transit, not the Larmor carrier.
description: No separate magnetostrictive period is extracted. Lab loops are sweep- and wall-limited.
notes: The 28 GHz/T Larmor carrier is owned by permanent-magnet-latch.

observed_text: Why λ_s spans 10⁻⁵ (Ni) to 10⁻³ (Terfenol-D) is not extracted from a node rule here. Crystal-field and magnetoelastic coefficients are taken as data, the same way d_33 is taken as data on piezoelectricity.
implied_text: The T_C and lattice-destruction collapses are located; λ_s is a handbook coupling.
description: Coupling magnitude is taken, not derived from a stated node-level spring. Mapping confidence is therefore medium.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch: do not re-specify remanence, T_C, or KV here.

observed_text: Saturation magnetostriction λ_s = ΔL/L: Ni λ_s ∼ 10⁻⁵ (negative); Fe polycrystalline average 10⁻⁵ class or smaller; Terfenol-D (Tb–Dy–Fe) λ_s in the 10⁻³ class.
implied_text: A saturation strain λ_s locked to the aligned moment, plus the inverse stress–M channel, while the ordered magnet and the lattice both remain.
description: The strain output is a material-typical λ_s class from ~10⁻⁵ (Ni) to ~10⁻³ (Terfenol-D), locked to aligned M.
notes: Volume magnetostriction is a separate, usually smaller, channel and is the Invar cancellation term owned by thermal-expansion. A particular polycrystal’s λ_s is medium (texture- and stress-dependent).

observed_text: No separate magnetostrictive latch. The thresholds are the host magnet’s: T_C, the anisotropy / coercivity write field, and the mechanical integrity of the grid. Magnetoelastic energy is an extra term in the anisotropy budget; it can raise or lower the latch barrier but is not the barrier’s origin in NdFeB-class K_1.
implied_text: This file must not re-specify the magnet. Strain is locked to M; the barrier that holds M is the latch’s.
description: Magnetostriction is a coupling, not a latch. T_C, KV, and coercivity stay with permanent-magnet-latch.
value_text: host T_C / coercivity / grid; not a second K_1
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch. Inverse (Villari) stress–M is a write / read channel on that latch.

observed_text: λ → 0 as T → T_C⁻ of the ordered magnet. Fe T_C ≈ 1043 K. Ni and Terfenol-D fail at their own, lower, Curie points. This is the same thermal cliff that erases net M on permanent-magnet-latch.
implied_text: T > T_C → ordered moment gone → λ = 0. This file owns the length change, not the latch.
description: Magnetostriction dies at the host Curie point with the ordered moment.
value_text: T > T_C (Fe ≈ 1043 K; Ni / Terfenol-D lower)
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch, which owns remanence, T_C, and KV. value_si is Fe T_C as the file’s numerical pin.

observed_text: Plastic deformation, cracking, or melting removes the lattice that carries ΔL. Severe shock can also scramble the latch via this coupling without a bulk melt.
implied_text: No grid, no λ. The mechanical failure path named on permanent-magnet-latch is this coupling plus ordinary plasticity.
description: Lattice damage ends ΔL and can write error into M without reaching T_C.
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch (lattice-shock row): the latch entry owns remanence erasure; this file owns the strain channel. Cross-cite melting for bulk grid loss.

observed_text: λ follows M(H) and saturates once the domain population is aligned. A small field on a hard magnet produces little λ until the write field is reached. Vanishing spin–lattice coupling (λ_s → 0) leaves the moment and does not change the length.
implied_text: Macroscopic ΔL is small if M is not aligned, even when λ_s is finite. Alignment is a domain / coercivity condition, not a second coupling.
description: Unaligned domains or a hard magnet below coercivity hide λ_s. λ_s → 0 is a different, material failure.
value_text: M not aligned (below write field); or λ_s → 0
notes: Cross-cite magnetic-domains and ferromagnetic-hysteresis.

observed_text: An ordered magnetic population sitting in a deformable lattice, large enough for a macroscopic ΔL and a macroscopic M. A paramagnetic crystal has the lattice and not the ordered moment. A liquid magnet (if any) has no static shear grid to register a linear λ_s of this kind.
implied_text: Hardware is ordered M plus a strain-carrying grid. Grain-scale latching of M is owned by permanent-magnet-latch / superparamagnetism; this file owns the strain that follows M.
description: Magnetostriction needs both an ordered moment and a deformable lattice. Either alone is not this machine.
notes: Cross-cite permanent-magnet-latch. Centrosymmetric iron is magnetostrictive and not piezoelectric.

observed_text: Expulsion on cooling through Tc is limited by thermal diffusion, eddy-current transients, and (in type II) flux-line motion — laboratory times, not the gap frequency 2Δ/h.
implied_text: This entry's static observation is the ω=0 expelled state. The gap frequency still sets the scale on which the condensate can respond to a changing field.
description: Static Meissner expulsion is not a 2Δ/h clock measurement; the expelled state is already the DC output.
notes: Contrast with josephson-effect, which owns the voltage-frequency lock.

observed_text: Cooling in a field yields B=0 rather than freeze-in. A hypothetical perfect conductor would trap the flux it already contained, not expel it. λ is a measured screening length, not a derived node count.
implied_text: QSA records expulsion as the stable output of the gapped state; it does not yet produce expulsion-versus-trapping from a more primitive update rule, and it takes λ as the hardware depth.
description: Why the equilibrium is expulsion rather than flux trapping is located as data, not derived from node rules. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Same kind of underived screening length as reflection's δ = λ/4πk.

observed_text: In the fully expelled state the volume susceptibility is χ=-1 (SI) and the interior induction is B=0, aside from a surface layer of depth λ.
implied_text: A field-free interior behind a surface layer of depth λ is the stable output of a fully provisioned screening buffer.
description: Complete Meissner expulsion is perfect diamagnetism of the expelled volume, held at zero continuous power.
notes: This entry owns field expulsion / λ. Superconductivity owns R=0.

observed_text: Complete expulsion (χ=-1, B=0 in the bulk) holds for type-I superconductors at H < Hc. Type-I Hc(0): Al μ0 Hc ≈ 10.5 mT; Pb ≈ 80 mT; Sn ≈ 30 mT. Type II: complete expulsion only for H < Hc1.
implied_text: Hc (type I) and Hc1 (type II) are the load-bearing field gates for complete expulsion. Holding the expelled state costs no continuous power.
description: Complete field expulsion is gated by Hc or Hc1, not by a static anisotropy latch.
value_text: H < Hc (type I; Pb ≈ 80 mT) or H < Hc1 (type II)
notes: value_si is Pb μ0 Hc. Type-II Hc1 and the mixed state are owned by type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: Type I: H > Hc → field floods and superconductivity itself collapses. Type II: H > Hc1 → complete expulsion fails (vortices enter) while R=0 can persist. H > Hc2 → condensate gone.
implied_text: Crossing the complete-expulsion gate is a Meissner failure even when the R=0 channel is still open.
description: The Meissner artifact dies at Hc or Hc1; that is not the same collapse as R=0.
value_text: H > Hc (type I) or H > Hc1 (type II)
notes: Split from superconductivity is required by the type-II mixed state. Hc2 is owned by type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: λ(T) and ξ(T) diverge as T→Tc; Hc, Hc1, and Hc2 fall to zero there. Warming through Tc ends the expulsion.
implied_text: Thermal closure of the parent gap sends the screening depth to infinity and the expelled state disappears.
description: Expulsion ends at Tc with the parent condensate.
notes: Material Tc values are tabulated on superconductivity. Type-I intermediate state from a finite demagnetizing factor is a shape-dependent partition, not a second condensate.

observed_text: Thin films with thickness d ≪ λ do not fully expel; the effective screening is incomplete. That is a buffer-starvation form of the same effect, not a different Tc.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning of the screening buffer leaves a nonzero interior field at any H < Hc1.
description: Films thinner than λ starve the expulsion layer.
notes: Analogous to reflection's few-nanometre continuity / penetration cliff, at a different length.

observed_text: London penetration depth λ(T) is the measured spatial buffer: B decays as e^{-x/λ}. Conventional elemental λ(0) sits in the 40–50 nm class (Nb and Pb near 40 nm; Al often quoted near 50 nm). YBCO λ_ab(0) sits in the 100–160 nm class.
implied_text: A superconducting layer at least of order λ thick is required before the interior field is fully expelled. This entry owns λ; superconductivity owns R=0.
description: Complete expulsion needs a screening buffer of tens of nanometres in conventional elements, of order 100 nm in YBCO's ab plane.
notes: value_si is the conventional-element mid-class. Precise λ(0) of any one film is medium (mean free path, surface, anisotropy). ξ and the vortex lattice are owned by type-ii-critical-field.

observed_text: Thermal vibration of the ions has a spectral ceiling at the Debye / zone-boundary clock. Melting is not that clock being exceeded. Nucleation and front propagation set the laboratory time to complete the conversion and are not a single material pin.
implied_text: The conversion clock is nucleation and front motion, unpinned. Exceeding Θ_D is not melting.
description: Melting is loss of restoring couplings, not Debye-clock overrun. No single laboratory conversion time is extracted.
notes: Pb: Θ_D ∼ 100 K, T_m ≈ 600 K. Diamond Θ_D class ∼ 2000 K; 1 atm solid sublimes rather than a tungsten-style melt.

observed_text: Lindemann criterion (conventional, not a derivation): the crystal is near melting when √⟨u²⟩/a ∼ 0.1–0.15. The number correlates with T_m across many solids; it does not predict T_m from node rules, and the prefactor is structure-dependent.
implied_text: QSA takes measured T_m as the empirical threshold. Lindemann is a displacement consistency check, not a derived barrier.
description: The mapping does not close on why ice, Al, and W fail at those temperatures. Lindemann is not a node-level derivation of T_m.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium while T_m data are High. Cohesive well depth, coordination, and anharmonicity (thermal-expansion) enter and are not yet primitive node specifications. Soft-mode melting belongs with phonon-dispersion. value_si is the 0.1–0.15 window midpoint.

observed_text: Below T_m, a solid with Bragg order and a shear modulus. At T_m, a first-order conversion whose temperature is a material constant at given pressure. Above T_m, a fluid without that grid.
implied_text: The stable product is the coexistence temperature itself plus the solid/fluid sides of the cliff.
description: The machine’s output is an ordered shear-carrying solid below T_m and a first-order conversion at the measured pin.
value_text: T_m(P) (ice 273.15 K; Al 933 K; W 3695 K at 1 atm)
notes: Clapeyron organizes dT_m/dP = ΔV/ΔS; ice ΔV < 0. It does not give T_m(P=0).

observed_text: Measured 1 atm melting points: ice T_m = 273.15 K; aluminum T_m = 933 K; tungsten T_m = 3695 K. These are empirical failure temperatures of the respective grids. The latent heat is the energy that must be supplied at coexistence. There is no simple anisotropy-style barrier KV from which T_m is computed in this mapping.
implied_text: The load-bearing threshold is the measured T_m: kT in the presence of the crystal’s cohesion is then sufficient to unbind the ordered grid.
description: T_m is the measured thermal gate of the grid, not a derived KV-style barrier.
notes: value_si left null: three empirical pins, not one universal T_m. First-order for these three: latent heat, volume jump, two-phase plateau.

observed_text: The grid can also be destroyed below T_m by large plastic strain, radiation amorphization, or dissolution.
implied_text: Those are lattice-destruction routes, not the thermal coexistence cliff.
description: Plastic strain, radiation, or dissolution can erase the grid without reaching T_m.
notes: Latch entries may list lattice destruction as a secondary failure; they own the latch, this file owns the grid.

observed_text: T → T_m at the ambient pressure → loss of Bragg order, loss of static shear, conversion to a fluid that carries only compressional sound. Superheating can temporarily overshoot T_m; the equilibrium collapse point remains the measured coexistence temperature.
implied_text: Thermal unbinding of the ordered grid at the measured coexistence T_m. Shear sound and static shear die with the solid.
description: The grid fails at T_m: Bragg gone, G → 0, only compressional sound remains.
notes: Cross-cite speed-of-sound (no shear in the melt) and elasticity (G → 0).

observed_text: A crystalline grid large enough to produce Bragg peaks and a macroscopic shear modulus. A few-atom cluster has no bulk T_m; a glass has no Bragg grid. Glasses and amorphous solids do not have this T_m cliff; their softening is a viscosity / timescale crossover.
implied_text: The sharp hardware is the ordered lattice itself, not a universal millimetre envelope.
description: Melting is a property of a Bragg-ordered, shear-carrying grid. Clusters and glasses are different machines.
value_text: Bragg grid + shear; no universal mm envelope

observed_text: 57Fe τ≈141 ns sets Γ. Lattice vibrations that kill f are Debye/phonon clocks.
implied_text: Nuclear lifetime plus host phonon clock.
description: Γ from nuclear τ; f from the grid clock.

observed_text: 14.4 keV is the line energy, not an under-threshold non-occurrence of this channel.
implied_text: Do not file as an energy-gate whose collapse is Eγ<14.4 keV.
description: Lattice-mode payload, not a 14.4 keV under-threshold gate.

observed_text: Recoilless resonant absorption, scanned at mm/s Doppler velocities.
implied_text: The lattice-enabled nuclear line is the output.

implied_text: Nuclear line plus lattice recoilless condition. Not an under-threshold 14.4 keV gate.

implied_text: Grid loss or hot <x²> is the collapse.
description: No recoilless fraction ⇒ no Mössbauer channel.

observed_text: A crystalline host that can take nuclear recoil as a whole. Free 57Fe has ER≈2 meV ≫ Γ≈4.7 neV and no overlap.
implied_text: The lattice is the buffer. A free atom is under-provisioned.

value_text: solid host; not a free atom

observed_text: Muon mean lifetime τμ = 2.197e-6 s (PDG 2026). Formation and fusion inside a formed dtμ ion sit far below that clock.
implied_text: τμ is the hard stop. Observation after the muon population is gone is not this effect.

notes: Lifetime taken from PDG, same honesty as me on pair-production.

observed_text: Zero muons after the beam is dark means zero catalysis. There is no remnant fusion cycle at zero muon population.
implied_text: This is not a 0 W latch. Identifying it with a defect-pinned interstitial cell is a mapping error.
description: Honest exclusion: μCF is a spent-node gate, not a hold-power memory.
value_text: not 0 W hold after muon gone
notes: Contrast membership on anisotropy-latch. Does not add a nuclear effect to the latch family.

observed_text: Dense d–t yields of order 100–150 fusions per stopped muon (Los Alamos / Jones class ~150). Products appear only while muons are present.
implied_text: Stable output is fusion-product yield per stopped muon, set by supply × cycle × (1−ωs), only while muons are present.
description: The machine emits a per-muon fusion yield, not a remnant cell at 0 W.
notes: value_si is the Jones LAMPF-class upper end. Not a net-energy factory number.

observed_text: mμ c² = 105.658 MeV; mμ/me ≈ 206.8. The muonic Bohr radius is ~a0/207, so dtμ / ddμ holds the nuclei close enough for fusion on a timescale below τμ.
implied_text: Not a latch. The muon mass rescales the well so the nuclear conversion occurs. The product leaves; the muon is recycled until it decays or sticks.
description: The gate opener is the muon mass ratio, not lattice strain and not KV.
notes: value_si is the muon rest energy. Q(dt)=17.6 MeV is the fusion release, not the gate that opens the cycle.

observed_text: Each muon is erased by decay at τμ or by α-sticking. dt sticking ωs is 0.5–0.6% class; dd sticking is ~10% class. Yield is ~100–150 dt fusions per muon.
implied_text: Sticking and decay cap the cycle. They are erase of the catalyst, not a latch blocking temperature.
description: Decay and sticking are the yield cliffs of this gate.
notes: value_si is the midpoint of the dt sticking class. Any one target’s exact ⟨n⟩ is medium.

observed_text: The same hydrogen-isotope target with no muons produces no catalysis cycle. Cosmic-ray flux does not become this cycle just because a hydride is present.
implied_text: Missing muon is the collapse of the effect. Lattice compression and H/M do not substitute for the node.
description: No muon ⇒ channel closed. Twin of pair-production’s missing recoil partner.
notes: This is the contrast to any muon-free LENR cell.

observed_text: One muon plus two hydrogen-isotope nuclei (a dtμ or ddμ ion) is the hardware for one catalysis cycle. A metal lattice is not required. Target density is capacity.
implied_text: N = 1 muon + two nuclei. No collective metal film and no defect-cell KV. Density raises the cycle rate; it does not open a muon-free cell.
description: The gate hardware is one muon and two hydrogen nuclei. Target volume is capacity.
notes: Same N=1 family as photoelectric, with a different particle.

observed_text: Bounce / dwell on the mm/s UCN scale (ms–s).
implied_text: Not a nuclear lifetime.
description: UCN bounce clock.

observed_text: The spacing is gravitational, not a pairing gap. No charge, no λ, no Tc.
implied_text: Do not fold into gapped-condensate. Same honesty as He-4.

observed_text: Stepwise transmission versus absorber height, first step at the z1 ~ 14 μm class.
implied_text: Discrete gravitational states as the stable output.

observed_text: Ground-state energy E1 ≈ 1.4 peV. Neutrons are selected as UCN, not thermalized into this well.
implied_text: Gravitational level spacing is the protecting gap. Family name gapped is loose.
description: peV gravitational ladder, not a pairing gap.

observed_text: Absorber below z1 passes essentially no ground-state neutrons. Neutrons that are not UCN are not bound.
implied_text: Under-height slit or wrong buffer collapses the steps.

observed_text: UCN plus a horizontal neutron mirror plus g. Ground-state height z1 ≈ 13.7 μm.
implied_text: The spatial buffer is the gravitational well height, not a metal film.

observed_text: The conversion, when allowed, is a high-energy QED process on timescales far below any laboratory clock. Subsequent slowing of the pair and annihilation are later steps.
implied_text: Pair-creation latency is not a laboratory-scale clock. Annihilation witnesses the conversion; it is not the gate.
description: The conversion, when allowed, is already complete on any laboratory clock.
notes: No numerical QED time is given; do not invent ħ/2mec².

observed_text: QSA takes me c² = 511 keV as a measured node specification. It does not here derive the electron mass from a more primitive resource count.
implied_text: The collapse clauses (Eγ < 1.022 MeV; no recoil partner) do not depend on that derivation.
description: The rest mass is located and measured; it is not derived from node rules.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; this clause is the underived step.

observed_text: Annihilation of a stopped positron on an electron returns two 511 keV photons. That line is the macroscopic witness that a pair was produced.
implied_text: A material- and energy-dependent pair yield above 1.022 MeV, followed by the 511 keV annihilation line, as the synchronized output of many independent photon–nucleus conversions.
description: The machine’s stable product is a pair yield plus the 511 keV line.
notes: value_si is one 511 keV photon.

observed_text: Rest energy me c² = 510.999 keV ≈ 511 keV. The pair gate in the field of a heavy nucleus is Eγ^th = 2 me c² = 1.022 MeV. Finite nuclear mass raises the exact kinematic threshold by a fractional ~ me/M, negligible for ordinary nuclei.
implied_text: The operating gate is the rest-mass sum 2me c². It is not the unbinding of a pre-existing electron. No optical photoelectric event opens this channel.
description: Pair production is a rest-mass creation gate, not an ionization gate.
notes: Forbidden below 2mec² even in a fully ionized plasma.

observed_text: A photon in free space, with no nearby mass to recoil, cannot satisfy energy and momentum together; the channel remains closed at every energy.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning closes the channel even for Eγ > 1.022 MeV.
description: Missing recoil partner is a spatial-buffer collapse, twin of the energy cliff.
notes: Two-photon pair production in an intense photon bath is a noted extension of the same rest-mass gate, not required for the nuclear-field case.

observed_text: Pair production on an electron (triplet production) opens only at 4 me c² = 2.044 MeV.
implied_text: An electron as the only recoil partner keeps the gate shut until 2.044 MeV. Same conversion, lighter momentum sink.
description: Wrong partner raises the rest-mass gate; it does not invent a second family.

observed_text: Below 1.022 MeV the pair channel is simply absent: no positrons, no subsequent 511 keV annihilation line from this process.
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of the effect.
description: Below 2mec² the pair gate stays shut.
notes: Photoelectric absorption and Compton scattering may still remove photons; they are other channels.

observed_text: One photon plus one nearby nucleus (or other recoil partner) is the hardware for one conversion. Isolated photons in empty space do not convert. A macroscopic rate then scales with nuclear column density.
implied_text: “Nearby” is a spatial-buffer condition: the photon must pass through the Coulomb field of a mass that can recoil. Empty space, however energetic the photon, is under-provisioned.
description: Hardware is one photon plus one recoil partner. The spatial clause is mandatory, not decorative.
notes: No Coulomb-radius length is given; do not invent one. Bethe–Heitler yield scales as Z², a capacity of the nuclear partner, not a second energy gate.

observed_text: Free-electron spin precession γ/2π ≈ 28.025 GHz/T.
implied_text: Baseline single-spin clock of the latch. Write/erase of a hard magnet is set by field sweep and wall motion, not this carrier.
description: The latch has a 28 GHz/T precession clock; holding the state does not require running that clock as a power draw.
notes: si_unit is Hz per tesla; value_si is the 1 T frequency.

observed_text: Technical coercivity is microstructure-dependent and much less than Ha ~7–8 T.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer/barrier specification for the mesoscale write threshold (nucleation, grain boundaries, dipolar coupling).
description: The latch-vs-soft and Tc/KV collapses do not depend on closing coercivity; the write field is still underived.
notes: File-level mapping remains High.

observed_text: A static magnet at rest produces no continuous I²R or hysteresis heat.
implied_text: Stable directional moment and static field/force at zero continuous power, inside the Tc / KV / lattice envelope.
description: Holding the latched state costs zero watts. Energy is the write/erase loop area only.

observed_text: Uniaxial anisotropy density K1 ≈ 4.5 MJ/m³; per-grain barrier ΔE ≈ K1V. Holding costs zero continuous power.
implied_text: Magnetocrystalline (or shape) anisotropy locks orientation. Energy is spent only on write/erase (hysteresis-loop area).
description: The latch exists because a barrier protects orientation at zero hold-power.
notes: Barrier energy is K1V, not K1 alone.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B Tc ≈ 585 K (312 °C). Commercial grades ~310–400 °C with Co substitution.
implied_text: kT exceeding the anisotropy barrier at Tc destroys phase coherence across the array → net-zero magnetization.
description: Thermal over-barrier collapse of the latch at the Curie point.

observed_text: Mechanical shock, plastic deformation, and decrepitation can destroy remanence without reaching Tc.
implied_text: Lattice / grain-structure failure writes error across the array by destroying the directional matrix.
description: The latch matrix is the crystal. Destroy the grid and the barrier goes with it.
notes: Lattice entry owns the grid; this row owns the latch erasure.

observed_text: KV ≲ 25 kT at operating temperature randomizes the grain on laboratory time.
implied_text: Same barrier, under-provisioned volume. Spatial-buffer twin of the thin-film mirror.
description: Too-small grains erase the latch thermally without reaching Tc.
notes: Primary owner of this collapse is superparamagnetism.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B K1 ≈ 4.5 MJ/m³. Laboratory stability convention KV ≳ 25 kT gives V ≈ 2.3e-26 m³ (~30 nm linear) at 300 K.
implied_text: A crystalline anisotropy cell large enough that K1V ≳ 25 kT is the latch hardware. Soft matrices lack this barrier.
description: The sharp hardware cliff is the grain-scale latch cell, not the sample envelope.
notes: 25 kT is a timescale convention, not a single experimental cliff. Cross-cite superparamagnetism.

observed_text: A usable motor force is F = ∇(m·B) from a large aligned population. There is no universal millimetre-scale cliff.
implied_text: Macroscopic force is synchronized output of many latched grains. Force scales with aligned moment; the sharp cliff stays at the grain.
description: The sample envelope is a capacity, not a second spatial cliff. No single minimum N for a usable force is extracted.
value_text: force scales with aligned m; no universal N

observed_text: Maximum phonon frequencies sit in the few-to-tens-of-THz class (Al’s spectrum ends near 10 THz; diamond’s near 40 THz). Si zone-centre Raman is 15.5 THz; diamond 40 THz (1332 cm⁻¹). Acoustic clocks run from zero up to the zone-boundary frequency of that branch.
implied_text: ω_s(q) is the allowed-clock table. Nothing in the lattice oscillates as a phonon faster than the highest measured branch.
description: The lattice’s mechanical clocks are the measured branches, from acoustic zero up to a material-typical THz ceiling.
value_text: few–tens of THz (Al ~10 THz; diamond ~40 THz)
notes: value_si is Al’s ~10 THz ceiling as a representative. Optical zone-centre pins: Si 15.5 THz; diamond 40 THz.

observed_text: QSA takes the measured ω(q) as data. Force-constant models that fit the curves are not promoted to node rules. The mapping does not predict which crystal will soften.
implied_text: Branch frequencies are located as the clock table but not derived from a more primitive set of node spring constants.
description: The allowed-clock map is taken, not computed from node springs. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium: hardware scale is not a single number; binary macros belong to related lattice entries.

observed_text: Inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering return discrete ω(q) peaks along each branch. Acoustic long-wave slopes match measured sound speeds (Al longitudinal ≈ 6.4 km s⁻¹; Si [100] longitudinal ≈ 8.4 km s⁻¹). Zone-centre optical pins include Si 15.5 THz and diamond 40 THz.
implied_text: The stable output is the measured surface ω_s(q), its long-wave speeds v_s, and its zone-centre optical frequencies, for as long as the crystal remains ordered.
description: The synchronized ion grid emits a material-typical allowed-clock map, not a single binary macro.
value_text: ω_s(q); v_s; Γ optical pins (Si 15.5 THz; diamond 40 THz)
notes: Long-wave slope is also speed-of-sound. Do not invent a single dispersion cliff.

observed_text: The harmonic restoring energy of a mode is ½ħω(2n+1) (or ½ku² classically). Softening to ω→0 is loss of that restoring constraint along one coordinate.
implied_text: This is an oscillator budget, not an activation barrier that holds a directional state. Dispersion is not a latch.
description: Phonon branches are driven oscillators, not a memory. There is no static barrier holding a written mechanical state.
notes: Negative latch spec: contrast with permanent-magnet-latch.

observed_text: Driving above the highest lattice frequency produces no additional phonon mode. Zone-boundary / reststrahlen / neutron cutoff sits at the few-to-tens-of-THz class. q outside the first zone is an alias, not a new clock.
implied_text: Drive faster than the last branch → no additional lattice mode.
description: The allowed-clock table ends at the zone-boundary maximum; faster drive is not a phonon.
value_text: ω above last branch (Al ~10 THz; diamond ~40 THz)
notes: Physical ceiling is owned here; Debye ω_D is the continuum stand-in filed under debye-cutoff.

observed_text: Loss of Bragg order ends the map. Melting or amorphization removes the discrete ω(q) branches. Finite lifetime / mean free path blurs a peak but does not erase the branch until the lattice itself fails.
implied_text: The clock table is carried by the crystal. Destroy the grid and the map ends.
description: Melting or amorphization erases the allowed-clock table by destroying the lattice that defined q.
notes: Primary owner of the thermal coexistence cliff is melting.

observed_text: A restoring branch can fall toward ω=0 as a structural transition is approached. An imaginary harmonic ω is the statement that the current lattice is mechanically unstable.
implied_text: Softening to ω→0 closes that restoring channel; a structural transition follows. This is not the first-order melting of Al or W.
description: A branch that loses its restoring frequency is a coordinate-specific grid instability, not the melting cliff.
notes: Soft-mode trajectories are high as a class and medium for any one crystal’s T-axis. Melting owns Bragg-order loss.

observed_text: One primitive cell already defines an optical zone-centre clock; a well-defined q is a phase relation across many cells. Amorphous solids retain a vibrational density of states but lose sharp ω(q) branches. There is no single nanometre cliff.
implied_text: The hardware is the crystalline lattice. The map as a spectrum is an extended-crystal object, not a 10–20 nm buffer.
description: Phonon dispersion requires an ordered grid; one cell sets an optical clock, but the spectrum is many-cell. Amorphization is loss of the map, not a thickness failure.
value_text: primitive cell + extended crystal; no nm cliff
notes: Contrast reflection’s connected-film buffer. Lattice constants in file: Si 5.43 Å; Al 4.05 Å; diamond 3.57 Å.

observed_text: Generation follows the optical cycle (femtoseconds).
implied_text: Generation, when allowed, is already complete on any laboratory shutter. Bias does not replace this clock; it only reads the carriers.
description: Pair generation latency sits in the femtosecond optical-cycle neighbourhood.
notes: Same generation clock class as semiconductor-gap-absorption.

observed_text: τ spans nanoseconds in many direct-gap or dirty samples to milliseconds in high-purity Si. No single universal τ is claimed. Chopping faster than 1/τ rolls off the photocurrent. Gain Γ = τ/t_tr multiplies the current; it does not move Eg.
implied_text: The readout clock is the recombination lifetime τ and the transit time t_tr. Gain is this pair of clocks written as a performance number.
description: τ is a performance metric, not a threshold. Clock overrun of the readout is not closure of Eg.
notes: value_si is a mid-class marker of the stated ns–ms window. Lifetime is high as a class and sample-specific as a number.

observed_text: QSA does not here derive τ from a primitive node count. Lifetime is taken as a measured recombination resource. Gain figures of a given detector are therefore performance data, not predicted constants.
implied_text: The threshold mapping does not depend on closing that derivation.
description: Eg is located; τ and gain are taken as measured performance, not derived.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; this clause is the underived step.

observed_text: A light-dependent conductance whose spectral onset tracks Eg or Et, with magnitude set by η, α, τ, and μ, reverting when generation stops. Δn = Gτ.
implied_text: Stable output is a reversible, light-dependent conductance, not a latched state and not an ejected vacuum current.
description: The machine’s product is Δσ(hν) that turns on at the gap and reverts when generation stops.
value_text: Δσ onset at Eg or Et; reverts when light off
notes: Photoelectric-threshold and work-function-thermionic eject the carrier into vacuum; this entry keeps it inside the solid.

observed_text: Intrinsic photoconductivity is gated by the same gaps as semiconductor-gap-absorption: Si Eg ≈ 1.12 eV, Ge ≈ 0.66 eV, GaAs ≈ 1.42 eV, diamond ~5.5 eV (all 300 K). Extrinsic photoconductivity is gated by a trap depth Et < Eg.
implied_text: The operating gate is Eg (intrinsic) or Et (extrinsic). Bias does not replace the gate; it only reads the carriers. Thermal generation across the same gate produces dark current.
description: Photoconductivity is the same Eg gate as gap absorption, read as current rather than as opacity.
value_text: Si Eg ≈ 1.12 eV (300 K); or Et < Eg extrinsic
notes: Must share this collapse energy with semiconductor-gap-absorption. value_si is Si at 300 K.

observed_text: τ too short → generated carriers vanish before they contribute a measurable Δσ. Absorption without photocurrent is allowed.
implied_text: The gate opened; the output did not last. That is a readout-clock failure, not a denial of Eg.
description: Clock starvation of the readout leaves the spectral gate intact.
value_text: τ too short vs t_tr / measurement
notes: Blocking contacts or a vanished bias likewise remove the current readout without closing Eg.

observed_text: Below Eg (or Et) this conversion does not occur. Below the edge, extra light of that colour does not raise the current through this channel. Conductance stays at the dark baseline.
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of the effect.
description: Below Eg the photoconductive gate stays shut.
notes: Sub-gap current, if any, is thermal, two-photon, or defect-assisted — other channels. Raising T buries Δσ in dark current: a thermal failure of readout, not a shift of the optical gate to zero.

observed_text: The conversion event is one absorbed photon promoting one electron (and a hole) across Eg or Et. There is no collective optical-buffer analogue of the 10–20 nm mirror. Thinning the absorber reduces the generation volume in proportion to 1−e^{−αL}.
implied_text: A measurable current is the summed drift of a large generated population between contacts. The crystal must be intact enough to support bands or defined traps, and contacted.
description: The gate is a single-event conversion inside an intact, contacted crystal. Thickness is a generation capacity, not a continuity cliff.
notes: Absorption without photocurrent (very short τ, bad contacts) and photocurrent without strong opacity (thin extrinsic layers) are both allowed.

observed_text: Streaking delays of tens to hundreds of attoseconds. Intensity sets rate, not one-event latency.
implied_text: The conversion is finished on any optical-cycle-averaged laboratory clock.
description: Single-electron conversion latency sits in the attosecond regime.

observed_text: Face dependence and contamination shift φ by tenths of an eV. QSA takes measured φ as the gate.
implied_text: No derivation of the 2–6 eV class from a surface-dipole plus chemical-potential construction.
description: The gate is located and shown to be a surface resource; its value is not derived from node rules.
notes: Do not identify φ with Ag’s 3.9 eV optical plasma edge.

observed_text: A material- and face-typical φ, zero photocurrent below it, linear Kmax(ν) above it.
implied_text: The stable output is the threshold itself plus the above-threshold kinetic-energy line.
description: The machine’s stable product is a work-function gate and a linear surplus-energy line.

observed_text: Typical φ 2–6 eV (Cs low, Pt high). KE = hν − φ above threshold.
implied_text: φ is the load-bearing gate. Below it (linear regime) conversion does not occur. Not a latch; the electron leaves.
description: The photoelectric effect is a single-particle energy gate at the work function.
notes: value_si is ~4 eV in joules, mid-class.

observed_text: hν < φ → no linear photoemission (only a Fowler tail exponential in (φ−hν)/kT).
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of the effect.
description: Below the work function the gate stays shut.

observed_text: A single conversion event is already the microscopic effect. Photoemission persists from atomically thin or adsorbate-covered emitters once hν clears φ.
implied_text: No collective buffer is required. One electron at a surface is the hardware. Escape depth limits collection, not the on/off of the gate.
description: Negative spatial-buffer spec: the gate is single-particle. Contrast with reflection’s 10–20 nm stack.
notes: How to query effects that do not need a spatial buffer.

observed_text: The mechanical side tracks the acoustic clocks of elasticity / speed-of-sound (transit across the plate). The electrical side tracks the dielectric response of the bound-charge population. Laboratory piezo devices are usually limited by the plate resonance, not by an atomic period.
implied_text: Device latency is the acoustic transit / plate resonance, not an atomic piezo clock.
description: No single atomic piezo period is extracted. Laboratory clocks sit at the plate resonance.
notes: Cross-cite speed-of-sound and refraction-dielectric.

observed_text: The mapping takes handbook d_ij as the coupling strength. QSA does not yet derive why quartz is ~2 pC N⁻¹ and PZT is 10² class from node rules.
implied_text: The symmetry gate and T_C collapse are located; the magnitude of d is taken, not computed.
description: Coupling magnitude is a handbook input. That is the principal reason the mapping is medium rather than high.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Polar latch is a different machine sharing the same crystal.

observed_text: Handbook coupling class: quartz and AlN sit in the single-digit to ~10 pC N⁻¹ class (quartz d_11 ≈ 2.3 pC N⁻¹ is a standard cut number); PZT ceramics sit in the 10² pC N⁻¹ class.
implied_text: A linear, reversible strain ↔ polarization conversion with a material-typical d_ij, present only while the inversion-free (and, if ferroelectric, polar) lattice holds.
description: The coupling output is a pC/N-class d_ij: quartz ~2, PZT ~10², only inside the symmetry / polar envelope.
value_text: quartz d_11 ≈ 2.3 pC N⁻¹; AlN ~1–10; PZT 10² class
notes: value_si is the quartz d_11 pin. A particular ceramic’s d_33 is medium (process- and composition-dependent). Specific commercial PZT grades are not a single pin.

observed_text: The existence gate is inversion-free lattice symmetry, not an energy barrier. Quartz is not a ferroelectric latch; its coupling tracks the non-centrosymmetric lattice, not a switchable remnant polarization. Coercive field writes the polar latch; it is not the piezo coupling itself.
implied_text: Linear piezo is a symmetry-gated coupling, not a memory. Ferroelectric remnant P is a different machine sharing some crystals.
description: No piezo latch. The gate is inversion-free symmetry; quartz does not die with a remnant-P write.
value_text: inversion-free gate; not a KV / P_r latch
notes: Ferroelectric T_C is an additional thermal threshold on the large polar d_ij. Cross-cite ferroelectric-remanence.

observed_text: The large polar d_ij of PZT / BaTiO3 vanishes with the polar phase above T_C (BaTiO3 T_C ≈ 393 K; PZT T_C is composition-dependent, typically a few hundred °C). Quartz α–β at 573 °C changes the coefficients; β-quartz remains non-centrosymmetric. Quartz does not die at a ferroelectric T_C.
implied_text: PZT fails as a large piezo at ferroelectric T_C even while a solid remains. Quartz fails only by losing the non-centrosymmetric grid.
description: Ferroelectric piezo has a T_C collapse of the large d_ij. Quartz does not share that cliff.
value_text: T > T_C (BaTiO3 ≈ 393 K; PZT few hundred °C)
notes: value_si is BaTiO3 T_C. Two collapse routes must not be collapsed into one sentence. Remnant P owned by ferroelectric-remanence.

observed_text: Lattice destruction (melting) removes the coupling with the grid. Cracking of the grid ends the coupling. Drive out of the linear window produces harmonics and, in ferroelectrics, depoling.
implied_text: No inversion-free solid, no linear d_ij. Shock-depoling or cracking is lattice damage, not a second copy of melting.
description: Melting or cracking destroys the strain–polarization hardware with the lattice.
notes: Cross-cite melting. Mechanical-lattice damage on the latch is not restated as a second melting.

observed_text: Centrosymmetric crystals have d_ij = 0 for the linear effect (Si, NaCl, most metals; or a phase that restored inversion).
implied_text: If inversion is a symmetry, the linear output is forbidden, independent of field strength short of breakdown.
description: Inversion present → d_ij = 0. As sharp a hardware condition as the plasma-frequency clock on reflection.
notes: Dielectric breakdown at high E is a different cliff (dielectric-breakdown).

observed_text: Linear piezoelectricity requires a lattice without an inversion center. Twenty of the 32 crystal classes meet that condition. A centrosymmetric crystal of any size does not provision the linear coupling. A crystalline or poled ceramic lattice must be large enough for a macroscopic stress and a macroscopic polarization to be defined.
implied_text: The hardware is an inversion-free grid. Size does not create d_ij if inversion is present. Polar memory of a poled ferroelectric is owned by ferroelectric-remanence.
description: The linear strain–polarization machine is provisioned only by a non-centrosymmetric lattice (20 of 32 classes).
value_text: 20 of 32 classes inversion-free; d_ij = 0 with inversion
notes: Centrosymmetric crystals may still show quadratic electrostriction, which is not this entry.

observed_text: Plasma periods: ~0.3 fs (Al, ℏωp≈15 eV); ~0.5 fs (Ag free-electron, 9 eV); ~0.7 fs (Na, 5.7 eV). Ag optical-edge period ~1 fs. Ionospheric cycle is microseconds.
implied_text: The electron population must complete a collective screening cycle within one drive period. Miss that cycle and the reflected beam collapses.
description: Clock is load-bearing. Metal screening finishes in a few 10^{-16}–10^{-15} s; the ionosphere on a microsecond scale.
value_text: 0.3–0.5 fs (Al / Ag free-electron); Ag optical ~1 fs
notes: value_si matches the Al–Ag free-electron band used on reflection. Ionospheric microseconds are the same rule at ~10^{17} lower density.

observed_text: ωp=√(ne²/ε₀ m) is the measured clock. A closed mapping would say why the collective cycle time is 2π/ωp from node rules alone.
implied_text: QSA takes measured ωp(n) as the clock specification; it does not derive that period from a more primitive node update.
description: Same class of gap as reflection taking λ/4πk as the buffer. Not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Ag’s interband shift is a coarseness of the simplest clock=ωp statement, not a second gap class. Contrast photoelectric-threshold: collective n vs single-electron φ.

observed_text: Below the edge, bulk reflectivity is high (polished Al ~90% in the visible; alkalis similarly metallic). Above it the bulk supports propagating modes and a previously opaque film transmits.
implied_text: A material-typical plasma or interband edge: high R below, transmission above, at zero extra power.
description: The synchronized electron gas emits a spectral gate, not a stored state.
notes: Bound-charge analogue of ω≫ωp is refraction-dielectric’s ε→1 X-ray limit.

observed_text: Operating condition is ω<ωp (Al ℏωp≈15 eV; alkalis 3.8–5.7 eV) or, in Ag, ω below the interband-shifted optical edge ~3.9 eV. No continuous external power beyond the incident field.
implied_text: Driven collective response, not a memory. ℏωp is an energy scale of the clock, not an activation barrier that holds a state.
description: The window is a clock ceiling, not a latch barrier.
value_text: ω < ωp (Ag: ℏω ≲ 3.9 eV); no latch
notes: Do not identify Ag’s 3.9 eV optical edge with Ag φ ~4.3–4.7 eV (photoelectric-threshold).

observed_text: Metals transmit when the drive exceeds the plasma (Al ℏωp≈15 eV, λp≈83 nm; Na 5.7 eV; K 3.8 eV) or Ag’s interband-shifted optical edge ~3.9 eV (~320 nm). Residual absorption remains; the cliff is loss of metallic reflection.
implied_text: Drive faster than the collective screening clock → the population cannot finish a cycle in one period → transmission.
description: This entry owns the ω>ωp collapse that reflection also lists. Same machine, failed by clock rather than thickness.
value_text: ω > ωp (Al ~15 eV; Ag optical edge ~3.9 eV)
notes: value_si is Al ωp/2π, as on reflection:above-plasma-edge. Al and alkalis are the clean test; Ag is interband-shifted.

observed_text: Ionospheric electron densities of order 10^{11}–10^{12} m^{-3} give plasma frequencies of a few to ~10 MHz. HF broadcast below that ceiling is returned; higher frequencies pass.
implied_text: Same ω>ωp gate in a dilute charged gas. Hardware is a column of free electrons, not a crystal.
description: The ionosphere is the low-density instance of the same clock failure, ~10^{17} below metal n.
notes: value_si is the ~10 MHz ceiling.

observed_text: A continuous stack on the order of the optical penetration depth (about 10–20 nm in Ag or Al). A discontinuous or ≲5–10 nm film never forms the collective response at any frequency.
implied_text: The cutoff is a property of an already-provisioned continuous metallic buffer. This entry owns the spectral collapse, not the thickness floor.
description: Same connected stack as reflection; starve the buffer and there is no plasma edge to fail.
notes: Spatial starvation ≲5–10 nm is owned by reflection. Carrier densities that feed ωp: Al ~1.8e29 m^{-3}; Ag ~5.9e28; Na ~2.7e28.

observed_text: Ionospheric electron densities of order 10^{11}–10^{12} m^{-3} — ~10^{17} lower than a metal (Al ~1.8e29 m^{-3}).
implied_text: The same clock rule runs in a dilute free-electron column. Hardware is density enough to set a radio-band ωp, not a 10–20 nm crystal stack.
description: Dilute-plasma hardware is a charged column at 10^{11}–10^{12} m^{-3}, not a metallic film.
notes: value_si is the geometric mean of the quoted decade.

observed_text: Thermal ramp of the crystal (seconds). Fusion is prompt.
implied_text: Clock is the pyro ΔT ramp, not τμ.
description: Seconds-scale ramp clock.

observed_text: No muon is required. A pulsed-coil hydride is not this accelerator.
implied_text: Do not identify with μCF or with the EM-LENR cell.
description: Polar-field beam gate, not a latch and not μCF.
value_text: not μCF; not the hydride cell

observed_text: 2.45 MeV D–D neutrons per thermal cycle, yield class ~10^3–10^5 (apparatus-dependent).
implied_text: Yield is a class, not a constant. Witness is the 2.45 MeV line.
description: D–D neutron burst per ramp.

observed_text: ~100 kV class pyro potential puts D in the tens-of-keV beam-target window. Lower potential collapses the D–D cross section.
implied_text: Stacked gates: pyro field, then ordinary D–D Coulomb barrier.
description: Tens-of-keV D beam opens D–D.

observed_text: No ΔT ⇒ no pyro field ⇒ no neutrons. No deuterium ⇒ no D–D neutrons.
implied_text: Missing field engine or missing D closes the channel.
description: No ramp or no D is the collapse.

observed_text: A pyroelectric crystal (LiTaO3 class) plus deuterium. Nuclear event is beam-target D–D.
implied_text: Polar crystal is the field engine; D is the nuclear fuel. No muon required.
description: Pyro crystal + D is the hardware.

observed_text: The cyclotron frequency ωc = eB/m is the field-set clock. ħωc is the Landau-level spacing. The Hall plateau is not itself a radiated frequency; it is a DC resistance that remains stable while that clock keeps the Landau ladder resolved against scattering and against kT.
implied_text: The same eB/m combination that cyclotron-resonance reads as an absorption line is here the clock that keeps the gap resolved so a DC plateau can exist.
description: QHE runs on a cyclotron clock; the output is a resistance plateau, not an absorption line.
notes: Cross-cite cyclotron-resonance, which owns the line.

observed_text: QSA takes RH = h/νe² from metrology. Filling ν = ns h/(eB) is bookkeeping, not a derivation of why RH equals that combination. Bulk gap plus edge path is the measured surviving hardware.
implied_text: QSA does not obtain h/e² from a node-count or buffer rule, and it does not yet specify why current is expelled to the edge and why that forces RH onto RK/ν. Fractional plateaus are explicitly unmapped.
description: The quantized Hall resistance is a universal output taken from metrology, not derived from node rules. That missing derivation is load-bearing.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Same class of gap as taking δ = λ/4πk as the mirror thickness, but here the output is a universal constant. No anyon or fractional-charge story is added.

observed_text: Quantized Hall resistance at integer plateaus: RH = h/(ν e²) = RK/ν, with the von Klitzing constant RK = h/e² ≈ 25812.807 Ω. On a plateau, Rxx → 0.
implied_text: A Hall resistance locked to RK/ν together with a vanishing longitudinal resistance, while the 2DEG, the perpendicular field, the temperature, and the current remain inside the envelope.
description: The stable metrological output is RH = h/νe² with Rxx → 0.
notes: Complementary lock to josephson-effect (2e/h). Fractional plateaus are a harder related case and are not the primary artifact.

observed_text: Plateaus survive only while kT and the Hall electric field remain small compared with the gap that the Landau-level spacing (plus the sample's disorder-broadened mobility gap) sets. Graphene in a large perpendicular field can still show integer plateaus near room temperature — the same gap-versus-kT constraint.
implied_text: The Landau-level (mobility) gap is the energy barrier that protects a plateau. The perpendicular-field condition is a field threshold that opens the gap; moving B so that ν sits between integers takes the system out of a gap.
description: A plateau is a gap-protected DC state: kT or a Hall field comparable to the gap collapses the quantization.
notes: Disorder that widens a plateau is a sample-dependent resource, analogous to pinning on type-ii-critical-field. Integer values of RH do not depend on closing it; the width of the flat region does.

observed_text: An in-plane field does not open this artifact. The field must be perpendicular to the plane.
implied_text: Wrong field orientation is a hardware-gate failure: the Landau ladder of this machine does not open.
description: In-plane B is a non-occurrence of the integer quantum Hall machine.
notes: Distinct from moving a perpendicular B off a plateau.

observed_text: Moving the field off a plateau destroys the flatness and restores a finite Rxx. Off the plateau, Rxx is finite and RH is not flat. Plateaus are centred where ν = ns h/(eB) sits near an integer.
implied_text: When ν is not in a gap, the protected edge-channel output is gone.
description: Off-integer filling is the field/filling collapse of the plateau.
notes: Filling ν = ns h/(eB) locates the plateaus; it is bookkeeping, not a derivation of RH = h/νe².

observed_text: Low temperature and modest current are required; raising either washes the plateaus out. The precise current and temperature at which a given sample leaves metrological flatness are medium (mobility- and geometry-dependent). Destroying the 2DEG (density or mobility collapsed) removes the integer ladder.
implied_text: Thermal population of adjacent levels, or Hall-field / current breakdown, collapses the gap protection. Buffer destruction is a coarser failure of the same machine.
description: High T or high current wash the plateaus out by overrunning the Landau/mobility gap.
value_text: kT or Hall field vs gap
notes: Graphene's high-temperature integer plateaus sit on the same gap-versus-kT clause and do not require a second family.

observed_text: Hardware window: a 2D electron system (Si inversion layer, GaAs/AlGaAs heterojunction, later graphene) plus a magnetic field perpendicular to the plane. A bulk 3D metal in the same B does not produce these plateaus. An in-plane field does not open this artifact.
implied_text: A two-dimensional electron buffer plus a perpendicular field is the measured architecture. Once the field opens a gap in the bulk of the 2DEG, the surviving current path is along the edges. QSA records this layered hardware; it does not derive the edge path from node rules.
description: Integer quantum Hall plateaus need a 2DEG and a perpendicular field; a 3D metal is the wrong buffer.
notes: Magnetic length ℓB = √(ℏ/eB) is the in-plane spatial scale set by B; no universal nanometre number is quoted.

observed_text: Fermi-velocity transit through the saddle. The staircase is DC.
implied_text: Not a cyclotron clock and not a Hall plateau clock.
description: Transit clock; DC output.

observed_text: No perpendicular B is required. Output is two-terminal 2e²/h, not Hall h/νe². The 0.7 feature is out of scope.
implied_text: Do not mint a tenth design that swallows QHE and QPC.
description: QPC is not QHE. 2e²/h is taken.

observed_text: G = n × 2e²/h with 2e²/h ≈ 7.748e-5 S.
implied_text: Taken Landauer output. Not RH = h/νe².
description: Two-terminal conductance steps at 2e²/h.

observed_text: 1D subband edges open one by one. Pinch-off closes the last mode. No pairing gap and no Landau gap.
implied_text: Subband edges are the gates.
description: Mode edges, not 2Δ and not ħωc.

observed_text: Pinch-off gives G→0. High T or a dirty/long channel washes the steps.
implied_text: Last-mode close, thermal smear, or lost ballistic buffer collapse the staircase.
description: Pinch-off / T / mfp are the collapses.

observed_text: Ballistic constriction of width ~ λF (tens of nm in a GaAs 2DEG), shorter than the mfp. No perpendicular B required.
implied_text: 1D saddle in a 2DEG is the buffer. A wide 3D metal is the wrong hardware.
description: QPC needs a ballistic ~λF constriction.

observed_text: Al ħωp ≈ 15 eV and Ag ħωp ≈ 9 eV give plasma periods ~0.3–0.5 fs. Single-electron streaking is attosecond.
implied_text: Collective screening and the phase-reversed re-radiation complete on the plasma-period timescale.
description: The electron population must finish the reflection cycle in a few 10^-16 to 10^-15 s; the image is already complete on any macroscopic clock.

observed_text: The penetration depth is δ = λ/4πk, and k is itself an emergent optical constant of the same electrons.
implied_text: QSA currently takes the measured penetration depth as the buffer specification; it does not derive that depth from a more primitive node count.
description: The spatial buffer is located but not derived from node rules. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; this clause is the underived step.

observed_text: Polished Ag reflects ≳95% in most of the visible; Al ~90%. No continuous external power to the metal beyond the incident field.
implied_text: Stable phase-reversed reflected beam with material-typical R(λ), at zero extra power.
description: The synchronized electron gas emits a macroscopic reflected beam without a hold-power budget.

observed_text: No continuous external power is required to maintain the reflected image beyond the incident field itself.
implied_text: Hold-power of the mirror is zero; the drive is the light being reflected.
description: The mirror is not a powered lamp. Continuous draw to hold R is zero.

observed_text: Operating window is ω < ωp (or Ag’s interband edge) plus a continuous film at least one penetration depth thick.
implied_text: This is a driven collective response, not a memory. There is no static barrier holding a latched state.
description: Reflection has an operating threshold on drive frequency and thickness, not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
notes: Negative latch spec: contrast with permanent-magnet-latch.

observed_text: Metals transmit when the drive exceeds the plasma (Al, alkalis) or the interband-shifted optical edge (Ag ~3.9 eV).
implied_text: Drive faster than the collective screening clock → the population cannot finish a cycle in one period → transmission.
description: The same machine that fails by buffer starvation at low thickness fails by clock overrun above the plasma / interband edge.
value_text: ω > ωp (Al ~15 eV; Ag optical edge ~3.9 eV)
notes: Cross-cite plasma-frequency-cutoff, which owns this collapse as its primary artifact. value_si is Al ωp/2π order of magnitude.

observed_text: Below roughly 5–10 nm of continuous film, reflectivity collapses and transmission rises. Islanded films fail at any nominal thickness.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning or a disconnected morphology starves the buffer and the mirror disappears.
description: The mirror dies when the connected node count falls below a few-nanometre continuity / penetration cliff.
notes: Percolation vs electromagnetic penetration are two routes to the same failure class.

observed_text: Optical penetration depth in continuous Ag/Al in the visible is about 10–20 nm.
implied_text: A continuous metal stack of that depth (~40–85 atomic planes) is the minimum connected buffer for a stable collective reflected beam.
description: Reflection requires a connected electron-gas volume on the order of the optical penetration depth; fewer planes starve the collective screening response.
notes: Plane count derived from (111) spacing; the measured quantity is the nanometre threshold.

observed_text: Electronic polarization follows the optical cycle (visible period ~2 fs). Ionic and orientational channels drop out as the drive frequency is raised; optical n is then smaller than the static index in polar media.
implied_text: The bound-charge population must track the optical cycle. Channels slower than the drive fall out of the synchronized response. Drive well above the electronic resonances leaves n≈1.
description: Visible electronic refraction completes on a ~2 fs cycle; slower polarization channels are already off the clock.
notes: Water is the split-channel example: static ε_r≈80 vs optical ε≈n²≈1.78.

observed_text: Clausius–Mossotti / Lorentz–Lorenz relate (ε_r−1)/(ε_r+2) and (n²−1)/(n²+2) to Nα. They do not derive α from node rules. There is no single measured buffer length at which refraction appears.
implied_text: QSA takes tabulated n(ω) and the X-ray δ as the contrast specification.
description: Contrast is located as Nα but α is not derived. That is a gap, not a contradiction.
notes: File-level mapping remains Medium.

observed_text: Sodium-D / nearby visible: water n≈1.333; fused silica n≈1.458; typical crown glass n≈1.52; diamond n≈2.42; dry air n≈1.0003. Optical dielectric constant tracks n².
implied_text: A stable, material- and frequency-specific n(ω) and the macroscopic Snell kink from synchronized bound-charge polarization.
description: The synchronized bound-charge population emits a tabulated n(ω) and a ray bend.
notes: value_si is the crown-glass class. total-internal-reflection is the geometry/index gate on this same n.

observed_text: The dielectric itself draws no continuous power.
implied_text: Hold-power of the refracting slab is zero; the drive is the incident field.
description: Continuous draw to hold n is zero.

observed_text: Zero continuous power and no stored directional state. Dry air at STP breaks down near 3e6 V/m; solids typically 1e7–1e8 V/m. Breakdown ends the insulating window.
implied_text: Driven collective response, not a memory. The high-field edge is a different machine class (dielectric-breakdown), not a sharper location of n.
description: Refraction has an operating window, not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
value_text: no latch; Ebd is a different family
notes: Cross-cite dielectric-breakdown. Do not file breakdown as the refraction cliff.

observed_text: Above the electronic resonances the remaining real index is n=1−δ with δ typically 10^{-6}–10^{-5} for condensed matter at a few keV. A geometric Snell bend is then no longer a laboratory-scale fact. Vacuum is N=0. n1=n2 gives no interface kink.
implied_text: ε→1 (X-ray, vacuum, or drive above the electronic resonances) starves contrast → the ray kink disappears.
description: The load-bearing spectral/density collapse is n−1→0, not a film-thickness cliff.
notes: value_si is the geometric mean of the quoted δ decade. X-ray n<1 grazing total external reflection is the same kinematic gate as TIR with inverted contrast; geometry owned by total-internal-reflection. Free-electron analogue is plasma-frequency-cutoff (ω≫ωp).

observed_text: Path through the contrast region ≪ λ yields a fringe-level phase shift 2π(n−1)d/λ, not a geometric ray.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning of path converts the Snell kink into a phase plate.
description: A too-short path is a spatial failure of the ray output, not a missing polarizable volume.

observed_text: A geometric Snell bend requires a path through the contrast region of order a wavelength or longer. A much thinner slab is a phase plate, 2π(n−1)d/λ. There is no single millimetre cliff.
implied_text: Hardware is a polarizable bound-charge volume plus a path long enough for accumulated phase to become a wavefront tilt. Vacuum (N=0) and X-ray δ→0 are under-provisioned contrast, not a missing metal stack.
description: Refraction has no few-tens-of-nm connected-metal floor. The spatial spec is path ≳ λ through nonzero contrast.
value_text: path ≳ λ; no single nm/mm cliff
notes: Contrast with reflection’s 10–20 nm Ag/Al stack. A thick dielectric can still show n−1≈0 if the nodes supply no contrast at that frequency.

observed_text: The optical cycle and the interband polarization response sit in the femtosecond neighbourhood of visible / near-IR light.
implied_text: Relative to any laboratory shutter the conversion, when allowed, is already complete.
description: Interband conversion latency sits in the femtosecond optical-cycle neighbourhood.

observed_text: Indirect-gap edges (Si, Ge, diamond) rise more slowly: the conversion also consumes or emits a phonon. Direct gaps (GaAs) open with the photon alone.
implied_text: Indirect conversion needs a lattice-clock resource just above threshold. That is an extra resource on the same Eg gate, not a second family.
description: The slower rise of α in Si and Ge is a phonon-clock requirement, not a different collapse energy.
notes: No ħω_ph number is given. A frozen lattice with no phonon occupancy would starve the indirect channel at threshold.

observed_text: QSA here takes the measured Eg as the specification. Urbach tails and excitons are recorded as measured softness, not extra mechanisms.
implied_text: No derivation of why a given crystal has the gap it has from node rules alone. The collapse hν < Eg does not depend on that derivation.
description: The gate is located; its value is not derived from node rules.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; this clause is the underived step.

observed_text: A material-typical absorption edge and the associated split between a transmitting window and an opaque band. Ordinary wafers are optically thick in the visible once above Eg.
implied_text: Stable spectral split — window below Eg, opacity above — whenever a photon population is presented to an intact gapped lattice.
description: The machine’s stable product is a crystal-typical absorption edge, not a stored state.

observed_text: Room-temperature gaps (300 K): Si Eg ≈ 1.12 eV (indirect); Ge ≈ 0.66 eV; GaAs ≈ 1.42 eV (direct); diamond ~5.5 eV.
