implied_text: Eg is the load-bearing gate. Direct gaps open with the photon alone; indirect with photon plus phonon. Temperature moves Eg; it does not replace it.
description: Gap absorption is a photoelectric-class energy gate relocated into a bulk crystal.
value_text: Si Eg ≈ 1.12 eV (300 K); Ge 0.66; GaAs 1.42; diamond ~5.5
notes: value_si is Si at 300 K. Photoconductivity must share this collapse energy. Low-T limits sit higher by tens to ~100 meV.

observed_text: The edge is a property of the intact crystal: melting or amorphizing the lattice destroys the sharp crystalline edge.
implied_text: Loss of crystalline order washes the sharp edge into a smeared amorphous spectrum.
description: Destroy the periodic grid and the gate’s sharp location goes with it. Lattice-resource failure, not a change of family.

observed_text: Below Eg the crystal has a transparency window. Below-threshold light is refracted and, at most, weakly attenuated by processes that are not interband conversion.
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of the effect.
description: Below Eg the interband gate stays shut.
notes: Urbach tails and excitons are softness of the same gate, not a second channel. Free-carrier/impurity absorption can hide the window without opening this conversion.

observed_text: The gate is a property of the periodic lattice: a filled valence band and an empty conduction band separated by Eg. A single unit cell already carries the gap; macroscopic opacity is the summed conversion over an optical path of order 1/α.
implied_text: Hardware is a gapped lattice, not a surface φ and not a collective optical buffer. Destroying crystalline order removes the sharp edge.
description: One unit cell carries Eg. Path length sets how much light is converted, not whether the gate exists.
notes: No numerical 1/α is given; do not invent an absorption length.

observed_text: Same magnetic clocks as the parent latch: precession at ≈ 28 GHz/T; write latency set by the field sweep and by reversal mode (coherent rotation vs curling / buckling in real needles).
implied_text: Geometry changes the barrier; it does not invent a new carrier frequency.
description: The shape latch uses the same 28 GHz/T precession clock as the crystal-K1 latch.
notes: File quotes ≈ 28 GHz T^{-1}, not the 28.025 figure of the parent latch.

observed_text: Uniform-ellipsoid N is an idealization. Real precipitates, lithographed bits, and films have nonuniform magnetization and stray-field concentrations at corners.
implied_text: Those corrections change the numerical switching field (the same mesoscale Hc gap as on the hysteresis file). They do not remove the aspect-ratio → 1 collapse.
description: Switching-field numbers remain mesoscale; the ΔN = 0 collapse does not depend on closing them.
value_text: H_c ≠ H_K of the ideal ellipsoid
notes: File-level mapping remains High. This entry owns the ΔN term only; shape and crystal anisotropy add when both are present.

observed_text: A strongly elongated particle remains magnetized along its long axis after the field is removed, even when K1 is small. Thin films of soft magnets lie in-plane unless a perpendicular crystal anisotropy exceeds the film demag term.
implied_text: Stable output is a uniaxial remanent direction locked to the long axis (or to the film plane), without a large magnetocrystalline K1.
description: The geometry barrier emits long-axis (or in-plane) remanence at zero hold-power.
value_text: M locked to long axis / film plane
notes: Perpendicular remanence appears only when a crystal or interface K exceeds ≈ (μ0/2)Ms².

observed_text: Holding the long-axis remanent state costs zero continuous power. Energy is spent to rotate M off the long axis (hard-axis or switching field of order HK ~ Ms ΔN).
implied_text: Stable long-axis remanence at zero continuous power, without a large K1.
description: Holding the shape latch costs zero watts.

observed_text: Magnetostatic energy-density scale (μ0/2)Ms² is of order 1–2 MJ/m³ in Fe (μ0 Ms ≈ 2.15 T). Kshape = (μ0/2) Ms² (Nt − Nl). Soft iron K1 is only ~10^4 J/m³ class.
implied_text: The barrier is magnetostatic and geometric. No large K1 is required. Holding the long-axis remanent state costs zero continuous power.
description: Shape alone can latch a high-Ms needle because the magnetostatic density matches a hard-magnet K1.
value_text: 1–2 MJ m^{-3} in Fe; K_shape = (μ0/2) M_s^2 ΔN
notes: Ni’s scale is several times smaller (μ0 Ms ≈ 0.6 T). value_si is the mid-class Fe magnetostatic density.

observed_text: Collapse of the geometry barrier: aspect ratio → 1 (sphere / cube class) ⇒ ΔN → 0. Needles and thin plates are the opposite limit.
implied_text: Isotropic shape removes the latch even at large volume and high Ms. This is the defining collapse.
description: A sphere or cube has no shape latch; ΔN = 0 is a sharp, checkable failure.
notes: Alnico-class magnets sit on this file; sintered NdFeB does not need shape because its K1 already exceeds the magnetostatic scale.

observed_text: Ms → 0 (T > Tc, or a weak moment) → magnetostatic scale collapses even for a needle. Fe μ0 Ms ≈ 2.15 T; Ni ≈ 0.6 T.
implied_text: The geometry barrier is proportional to Ms². Lose the moment and the needle stops being a latch.
description: Shape anisotropy dies with Ms, whether by Curie collapse or by a weak-moment material.
notes: Thermal volume clause Kshape V ≳ 25 kT is the same form as superparamagnetism with K = Kshape.

observed_text: Demagnetizing factors of a uniformly magnetized ellipsoid: Nx+Ny+Nz = 1. Sphere: N = 1/3 on every axis, so ΔN = 0. Infinite needle: Nt−Nl → 1/2. Thin film: N⊥ → 1, N∥ → 0.
implied_text: The latch cell is a ferromagnetic body with nonzero ΔN whose volume still satisfies Kshape V ≳ 25 kT. A sphere has no geometry barrier at any size.
description: Shape latch hardware is an anisotropic body (needle or plate), not a unit cell and not a sphere.
notes: The particle or precipitate is the cell. A needle still fails if Kshape V cannot beat kT.

observed_text: The same free-electron population that screens optically on a plasma-period (femtosecond) scale screens a 60 Hz field over millimetres. Raising ω shrinks δ. ω→0 sends δ→∞.
implied_text: The low-frequency clock constraint is magnetic diffusion / charge relaxation across the conductor, set by measured σ and μ.
description: Skin is the same screening machine as reflection, run in the magnetic-diffusion band rather than on the plasma period.
value_text: 60 Hz class (power); δ shrinks as ω rises
notes: Cross-cite reflection (optical plasma period) and plasma-frequency-cutoff (high-frequency end). 60 Hz is the handbook operating point, not a universal clock cliff.

observed_text: QSA takes δ=√(2/ωμσ) as the buffer specification. It does not derive the square-root from a more primitive node count.
implied_text: The spatial buffer is located (classical δ, under local Ohm) but not derived from node rules.
description: Same class of gap as reflection taking λ/4πk: the length is measured, then used as the hardware spec.
notes: File-level mapping remains High.

observed_text: AC current is confined to a surface layer; AC resistance of a wire rises once a is no longer ≪δ. In the thick limit the effective cross-section is a ring of thickness ~δ.
implied_text: Frequency-dependent confinement of AC current, and the associated rise in AC resistance, from collective screening.
description: The synchronized electron gas emits a screened interior and a δ-thick current sheet.
notes: cyclotron-resonance (Azbel–Kaner) uses this skin layer as the only volume the microwave field occupies.

observed_text: The metal requires no auxiliary power beyond the current itself.
implied_text: Driven dissipative response, not a latch and not a gapped condensate. No static barrier holds a screened interior.
description: Skin has an operating window on ω and thickness, not an energy barrier that stores a written state.
notes: Meissner replaces this dissipative skin with a static London depth — different family.

observed_text: Classical δ assumes ℓ≪δ. When ℓ≳δ (high-purity cryogenic metals, microwave/radio) the local-σ length ceases to be the right buffer. Extreme anomalous scaling is δ∼ω^{-1/3}.
implied_text: Mean-free-path over-run takes the machine out of the classical-δ specification into a different operating length.
description: Anomalous skin is a local-response failure of the classical buffer, not a second millimetre cliff.
notes: Numerical ℓ of any one sample is medium (purity/T). Keep classical, anomalous, and optical lengths distinct.

observed_text: ω→0 sends δ→∞: DC current is uniform across the cross-section.
implied_text: Drive slower than the diffusion clock of any laboratory conductor → the skin/core contrast disappears.
description: The low-frequency collapse is uniform fill. Same machine as reflection, failed by a too-slow clock rather than a too-fast one.
notes: Twin of plasma-frequency-cutoff: that entry owns ω>ωp; this entry owns ω→0.

observed_text: A conductor whose radius or half-thickness a≪δ is an AC conductor with no skin/core contrast — the whole cross-section participates.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning relative to δ: the responding node count occupies the entire cross-section and the macroscopic skin is absent.
description: The spatial twin of reflection’s thin-film cliff, written against classical δ rather than optical λ/4πk.
notes: At 60 Hz in Cu the comparison length is 8.5 mm; at 1 GHz it is 2 μm. Cross-cite reflection for the optical 5–10 nm floor.

observed_text: Room-temperature copper (σ≈5.8e7 S/m): δ≈8.5 mm at 60 Hz; 2.1 mm at 1 kHz; 66 μm at 1 MHz; 2 μm at 1 GHz. Classical δ=1/√(π f μ σ).
implied_text: A conducting volume at least of order δ thick is required before a distinct screened interior exists. The buffer is the screening length, not a fixed millimetre.
description: Skin hardware is thickness ≳ δ(ω). The same metal is millimetres at power frequency and micrometres at radio frequency.
notes: value_si is the 60 Hz Cu handbook edge. Optical λ/4πk (~10–20 nm) is owned by reflection; London λ by meissner. Do not collapse the four lengths.

observed_text: Measured long-wave structure: v_s = √(C/ρ). Dry air at 20 °C, 1 atm: ≈ 343 m s⁻¹. Liquid water near 20 °C: ≈ 1480 m s⁻¹. Common steels, longitudinal: ≈ 5000–6000 m s⁻¹. Crystalline solids as a class sit in the kilometres-per-second range.
implied_text: The long-wave clock speed is the q→0 slope of the acoustic branch on the same grid phonon-dispersion maps at finite q. No single v_s is universal.
description: Sound speed is the material-typical √(C/ρ) slope, not a universal constant.
value_text: v_s = √(C/ρ); air ~343 m/s; water ~1480 m/s; steels 5–6 km/s
notes: value_si left null: the file lists class examples, not one pin. Air tracks √(γRT/M) with γ ≈ 1.4; water does not follow that gas law.

observed_text: Transit time on a path L is t = L/v_s. Relative to a human clock a laboratory path is still delayed: milliseconds in air across a room, microseconds in a metal bar of similar length. That clock is orders of magnitude slower than the zone-boundary / Debye clock of the same solid (terahertz class).
implied_text: The macroscopic acoustic clock is the transit L/v_s and the period λ/v_s, not the Debye ceiling.
description: A laboratory path is a millisecond (air) or microsecond (metal) delay; the same solid’s zone-boundary clock is THz.
value_text: t = L/v_s; ~ms in air across a room; ~µs in a metal bar
notes: Not a single material pin. Cross-cite debye-cutoff for the short-wave ceiling.

observed_text: A closed mapping would say why a given solid has the C it has, from node-spring rules, rather than taking handbook moduli as input. The speed measurement does not depend on closing it.
implied_text: QSA takes measured C and ρ and reads v_s = √(C/ρ). It does not derive the moduli from node springs.
description: The slope is located; the springs that set C are not derived here. Same gap as elasticity.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Ideal-gas air and condensed water share the Newton–Laplace form on different hardware; ideal-gas-pressure owns the wall force, not this slope.

observed_text: A material-typical, frequency-independent (long-wave) pair {v_L, v_T} in a solid, or a single v_L in a fluid. Examples: air ≈ 343 m s⁻¹; water ≈ 1480 m s⁻¹; steels 5000–6000 m s⁻¹.
implied_text: The synchronized long-wavelength output of the coupled mechanical population is that material-typical slope set.
description: The machine emits a handbook v_s class, not one universal speed.
value_text: {v_L, v_T} solid; v_L fluid (air ~343 m/s; steels km/s)
notes: Same springs as elasticity, read as a slope. qa ~ 1 moves the mode onto the phonon-dispersion curve.

observed_text: The operating condition is a finite restoring modulus (bulk, and shear if a shear wave is claimed) plus a density. The wave is a launched collective oscillation, not a memory.
implied_text: No latched barrier. Presence of C and ρ provisions the slope; holding a sound field is not a zero-power memory.
description: Sound is a driven collective oscillation of coupled nodes, not a stored directional state.
value_text: finite C and ρ; no latch

observed_text: Shear (transverse) sound exists in solids. It is absent as a propagating mode in liquids and gases at ordinary acoustic frequencies, where the shear modulus G = 0. Melting of a crystal is the same shear-branch collapse.
implied_text: G = 0 means the shear restoring couplings are not provisioned. The compressional branch can remain.
description: No shear modulus, no shear wave. Melting is that collapse of the solid’s shear branch.
notes: Cross-cite melting. Dissipative attenuation is a different, non-modulus cliff.

observed_text: A vacuum has no coupled mechanical medium: v_s is undefined there, not a small number. A density so low that couplings do not form a collective wave on the path also produces no sound.
implied_text: No nodes, no wave. Vacuum is missing hardware, not a limiting speed of zero.
description: Sound dies when the coupled medium is absent. v_s is undefined in vacuum.

observed_text: The continuum slope is stable only for λ ≫ a (lattice constant or mean spacing). A vacuum has no coupled mechanical medium. A fluid has compressional couplings and no shear restoring couplings.
implied_text: Hardware is a coupled mechanical population with many nodes per wavelength, plus the relevant restoring modulus. There is no single nanometre-scale thickness cliff.
description: Sound requires a medium and the modulus that provisions the claimed branch. Vacuum has no nodes; fluids do not provision shear.
value_text: λ ≫ a; medium + modulus; no nm cliff

observed_text: No separate clock beyond the wall-equilibration window and the spectral content already fixed by kT/h. The T^4 law is a time-averaged power.
implied_text: A detector faster than the wall exchange, or a surface whose T is not itself stable, does not report σT^4.
description: The T^4 reading inherits the wall averaging window and the spectral clock of the Planck curve.
notes: Clock inherited from blackbody-spectrum and thermal-equilibrium-temperature. k and h are defined.

observed_text: σ = 2π^5 k^4/(15 c^2 h^3) is a combination of defined constants. Finite-size corrections confirm that area and λ_max are the spatial resources and do not yield a single universal area.
implied_text: The mapping’s job is the T^4 envelope and its failures, not a re-derivation of the prefactor.
description: σ is defined; no universal radiating area is extracted. That is inherited from the spectrum entry.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Thermionic emission from the same hot surface is a charged-particle gate, not this photon-current integral.

observed_text: A hot black surface radiates a hemispherical exitance j = εσT^4. Doubling T multiplies the exitance by sixteen.
implied_text: The T^4 exitance is the power-meter reading of a black thermal surface — the frequency integral of the Planck curve.
description: Relabel the T^4 law as the integrated output of the thermal electromagnetic population. The prefactor is not a QSA extraction.
notes: σ = 5.670374e-8 W m^{-2} K^{-4} is defined from h, k, and c. Extracting σ as an independent machine constant would double-count those defined constants.

observed_text: None holding a latched state. A high-reflectivity metal is a resource failure of the black boundary condition (ε collapsed), not a stored configuration.
implied_text: Low ε is not a memory. The operating condition is a black (or grey) surface, not a barrier.
description: Stefan–Boltzmann has a black-boundary operating condition, not an energy barrier that stores a state.
notes: Cross-cite reflection.

observed_text: Surface not black (ε(ν)≠1 across the Wien band) → reduced or non-T^4 output. A grey surface still follows T^4 with a reduced prefactor; a selective surface does not.
implied_text: The extra collapse of the integral is a boundary-condition failure of the same electromagnetic population, not a new machine.
description: Non-black or selective surfaces take the power meter off σT^4.
notes: The same surface can be nearly black in the thermal infrared and reflective in the visible.

observed_text: Object or cavity not large compared with λ_max(T), or modes under-populated → the integral of a non-Planck spectrum is not σT^4. Finite-size / diffraction corrections appear in that regime.
implied_text: Area and λ_max are the spatial resources of the integral, for the same reason a sparse cavity leaves the Planck curve.
description: Undersized radiators fall off the T^4 envelope.
notes: Cross-cite blackbody-spectrum. No universal area is attached.

observed_text: As T→0 the radiated power vanishes into the instrument floor. Net exchange between two black surfaces is σ(T1^4−T2^4).
implied_text: Shrink the thermal resource and the photon current disappears. An undefined wall T is the same inherited collapse as the temperature entry.
description: T→0, or an unstable wall T, kills the T^4 reading.
notes: At 300 K, σT^4 ≈ 459 W m^{-2} is arithmetic from defined σ, not a machine number.

observed_text: The surface must present ε≈1 across the Wien band, and the radiating object must be large compared with λ_max(T), or the output is not σT^4. There is no single universal size cliff; the required area tracks T.
implied_text: Same statistical electromagnetic population as the blackbody spectrum, now read as one integrated current. Small or few-mode objects fall off the T^4 envelope for the same reason a sparse cavity falls off the Planck curve.
description: The hardware is a black-enough, large-enough radiator. No universal area is extracted.
value_text: ε≈1 on Wien band; size ≳ λ_max(T); no universal area
notes: At 300 K, λ_max ∼ 10 μm. Finite-size and near-field corrections are real; they do not yield a single area number.

observed_text: The spectroscopic gap sets a frequency scale 2Δ/h of order 10^11 Hz for conventional metals (Δ in meV) and higher in cuprates. AC dissipation rises as the drive approaches that scale.
implied_text: DC zero resistance is the ω→0 output of a gapped condensate that still has an internal clock at 2Δ/h.
description: The condensate clock sits near 10^11 Hz in conventional metals; laboratory DC is already slow compared with that scale.
notes: Cuprate gaps sit higher. This is not a voltage-standard lock; that lives on josephson-effect.

observed_text: The coherence length spans three orders of magnitude across materials. Vortex pinning — the mesoscale reason R=0 can outlive complete expulsion — is not specified by Tc or Δ alone.
implied_text: QSA does not have a single buffer number for the condensate, and it does not yet have a buffer/barrier specification for the pinning step that protects R=0 after Meissner has failed.
description: The T/H/I collapses are located; hardware identity and mixed-state pinning are recorded as gaps rather than filled.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium for these two gaps. This entry does not assert a pairing mechanism.

observed_text: Below Tc the DC electrical resistance falls below the instrument floor. A closed superconducting loop carries a persistent current for years with no measurable decay and no continuous voltage.
implied_text: Stable R=0 transport, and a persistent loop current at zero continuous voltage, inside the T / H / I envelope.
description: Superconductivity owns the R=0 artifact. Holding a persistent current costs zero continuous voltage.
notes: Split rule: meissner owns field expulsion / λ. Fluxoid integer is owned by flux-quantization.

observed_text: Tunneling and infrared absorption show a threshold 2Δ(T) that closes as T→Tc. The weak-coupling BCS ratio 2Δ(0)/kTc ≈ 3.52 is a fit to many conventional superconductors (Al close; Pb ~4.3).
implied_text: 2Δ is the energy threshold that suppresses ordinary quasiparticle transport. kTc, μ0 Hc (or Hc2), and the specimen Ic are the macroscopic envelopes that close that gap.
description: Zero resistance is protected by a measured gap that vanishes at Tc; the BCS ratio is a fit, not a universal node rule.
notes: Cuprates and other families that leave this ratio are not treated as contradictions. Pairing mechanisms are not QSA content.

observed_text: Type I: Al μ0 Hc ≈ 10.5 mT; Pb ≈ 80 mT; Sn ≈ 30 mT. Type II technical class: NbTi μ0 Hc2(4.2 K) ≈ 11 T; Nb3Sn μ0 Hc2(0) ≈ 25–30 T; YBCO μ0 Hc2,ab(0) of order 10^2 T.
implied_text: H > Hc (type I) or H > Hc2 (type II) destroys the condensate and restores finite R. Between Hc1 and Hc2, complete field expulsion has already failed while R=0 can still hold if vortices are pinned.
description: Field collapse of the condensate sits at Hc or Hc2; Meissner can fail earlier without ending R=0.
value_text: H > Hc (mT, type I) or Hc2 (tesla-scale, type II)
notes: value_si is NbTi μ0 Hc2(4.2 K). This entry owns R=0; meissner owns expulsion. Cross-cite type-ii-critical-field for the mixed-state window.

observed_text: Critical current Ic (or density Jc) is real and sharp on a given specimen, but it is not a material constant. It depends on cross-section, pinning landscape, field, and temperature. No single handbook Ic is quoted.
implied_text: I > Ic produces dissipation by pair-breaking, hot spots, or flux flow. That is a current-budget failure of the coherent channel.
description: Zero resistance ends when the transport current exceeds the specimen Ic. There is no universal current number.
notes: In type II the current cliff is often depinning rather than pair-breaking. Pinning itself is the consistency-gap row.

observed_text: Nb Tc = 9.25 K; Pb 7.2 K; Sn 3.72 K; Hg 4.15 K; Al 1.18 K; MgB2 39 K; YBCO ≈ 92 K; cuprates at ambient pressure extend to ~135 K (Hg-1223).
implied_text: T > Tc closes the gap and restores finite R.
description: Thermal collapse of zero-resistance transport at the material-specific critical temperature.
notes: These are material numbers, not a single universal Tc. value_si is Nb.

observed_text: Coherence-length class: Al ξ0 ~ 1.6 μm; Nb ξ0 ~ 40 nm; YBCO ξ_ab ~ 1.5–2 nm. Granular films and nanowires lose zero resistance when the coherent cross-section is under-provisioned.
implied_text: A coherent superconducting volume of order ξ in each direction is the buffer. That is a class, not a single measured cliff analogous to the 10–20 nm mirror.
description: Superconductivity needs a coherence-length buffer, but QSA does not have one hardware number for the condensate.
notes: value_si is Nb ξ0 ~ 40 nm, mid-class among the quoted materials. Closed-loop persistent current is owned by flux-quantization.

observed_text: There is no Josephson voltage-frequency lock (no e). Weak-link apertures in helium do produce an analogous current-phase oscillation; that is a related observation, not the primary artifact here. Second sound is a temperature wave in the two-fluid bookkeeping.
implied_text: Second sound is a hydrodynamic clock of the already formed superfluid, not the clock that opens the λ-point.
description: Superfluid 4He has no 2e/h lock; its internal hydro clock is not the Tλ specification.
value_text: no 2e/h lock; second sound is hydro
notes: Aperture analog belongs here as a related observation; the electrical specifications stay on josephson-effect.

observed_text: The load-bearing collapse is loss of ρs at Tλ (and of superflow at vc), not a measured charge gap of the superconducting kind. Why the λ-point sits at 2.17 K is not derived from node rules.
implied_text: The family name gapped is slightly loose here. The assignment follows the taxonomy rule — protected collective mode with a critical temperature — not a pairing-gap identification.
description: Chargeless superflow sits in gapped-coherence by collapse type, not by a pairing gap. The numerical origin of Tλ is also open.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Two-fluid bookkeeping is not used to derive Tλ. Dense interacting 4He is not the same hardware as a dilute alkali BEC.

observed_text: Circulation around a closed superfluid path is quantized: κ = h/m4 ≈ 9.97e-8 m²/s. Quantized vortices in the rotating liquid carry this increment.
implied_text: The chargeless counterpart of Φ0 is the circulation quantum h/m4 on a closed path.
description: Superfluid 4He emits an integer winding with measured quantum h/m4.
notes: Cross-check with flux-quantization is the existence of an integer winding, not identity of the two constants.

observed_text: Persistent currents circulate in a closed torus on laboratory timescales. Viscosity through a fine channel → 0 for the superfluid fraction below Tλ.
implied_text: Stable chargeless superflow and a persistent circulating integer at zero continuous power, inside T < Tλ and v < vc.
description: Holding superflow costs zero watts. The fountain and superleak responses are the same dissipationless output.
notes: Fountain head and vanishing viscosity are the same machine class. Contrast with BEC, which needs continuous cooling and trapping.

observed_text: Tλ = 2.17 K at saturated vapour pressure. The heat capacity has a λ-shaped singularity there. ρs → 0 as T → Tλ−, and ρs/ρ → 1 as T → 0.
implied_text: Tλ is the thermal cliff: ρs vanishes and the superleak / fountain / persistent-current responses go with it. Neither Tλ nor vc is a static anisotropy barrier; holding a persistent current still costs no continuous power while T < Tλ and v < vc.
description: The load-bearing thermal gate of chargeless superflow is the λ-point at 2.17 K.
notes: Under pressure the λ-line moves and ends when the liquid freezes. Two-fluid language is bookkeeping of ρs(T), not two substances.

observed_text: Above the λ-point the same liquid is an ordinary (if cryogenic) fluid: the superleak clogs, the fountain stops, and a finite viscosity returns.
implied_text: T > Tλ sets ρs = 0 and ends every superfluid response.
description: Thermal collapse of chargeless superflow at 2.17 K.
notes: Solidification across the melting curve is a coarser hardware removal.

observed_text: Superflow collapses above a critical velocity vc. Observed vc is geometry-dependent (channel size, film thickness, wall condition) and typically lies far below the Landau estimate taken from the roton minimum.
implied_text: vc is a velocity threshold that dumps superflow into a dissipative channel (vortex nucleation / coupling to the normal fraction), even though T < Tλ.
description: Superflow has a channel-dependent velocity cliff inside the T < Tλ envelope.
notes: Existence of a velocity cliff is high confidence; any one numerical vc is medium and is not quoted as a universal number.

observed_text: A connected volume of liquid 4He below Tλ, large enough to support a nonzero ρs. Superflow through packed powder and fine capillaries, and a climbing film, are the macroscopic demonstrations. There is no charge, no London λ, and no Meissner expulsion.
implied_text: The condensate buffer is a connected superfluid volume. The superleak or film is apparatus that the normal fraction cannot pass — a spatial filter, not the condensate buffer. Quantized circulation requires a closed path.
description: Chargeless superflow needs connected 4He with ρs > 0; it does not need an electromagnetic screening depth.
notes: Vortex cores are the chargeless analog of mixed-state defects. Do not collapse this hardware with dilute alkali BECs.

observed_text: Néel–Arrhenius attempt time τ0 is empirically 10^{-10}–10^{-12} s. Thermal escape attempts run on that scale (~10^{-11} s).
implied_text: In a stable grain the attempts bounce off the barrier. In an under-volume grain they succeed inside τm and rewrite the directional state at random.
description: The failure clock of the latch is the Néel attempt time, not the 28 GHz/T precession carrier.
notes: Single-spin precession remains ≈ 28 GHz T^{-1}; that carrier is not the failure clock.

observed_text: Real coercivity is not Ha, and real K of a nanoparticle is not the bulk K1. Surface anisotropy, grain-boundary structure, and dipolar coupling sit between unit-cell anisotropy and observed TB.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer/barrier specification for that mesoscale Keff step.
description: The volume-and-time collapse does not depend on closing nanoparticle Keff; the mesoscale step remains underived.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Brownian relaxation in a fluid is a different machine and is not this entry.

observed_text: Holding the unblocked state costs no continuous power; the directional memory is simply gone. Zero continuous power on the blocked side as well.
implied_text: Neither the fluctuating unblocked ensemble nor the blocked parent latch draws hold power.
description: Holding either side of the blocking contour costs zero watts.

observed_text: On the unblocked side, coercivity and remanence collapse to zero; M(H) is reversible and Langevin-like. A blocking contour TB(V, τm) recovers the loop below it.
implied_text: Stable unblocked output is a zero-remanence ensemble curve plus the blocking surface, not a motor moment.
description: The unblocked grain emits a reversible Langevin curve and a blocking contour, not a usable remanent force.
notes: A single unblocked grain’s fluctuating moment is not a usable motor; the Langevin curve is already an ensemble average. Blocked side is the parent latch.

observed_text: Uniaxial barrier ΔE ≈ K1 V. Nd2Fe14B K1 ≈ 4.5 MJ/m³. Superparamagnetism is that barrier times an insufficient V, compared with kT ln(τm/τ0).
implied_text: This is not a different barrier from the permanent-magnet latch. Collapse is under-provisioned volume at fixed K and T.
description: The same KV barrier holds a bulk grain and fails a nanoparticle; only V has changed.
notes: Cubic magnetite |K1| ≈ 1.35e4 J/m³; do not substitute |K1|V as if it were the uniaxial barrier. Shape anisotropy can dominate Keff in non-equant grains.

observed_text: KV ≲ kT ln(τm/τ0) (laboratory convention KV ≲ 25 kT) → remanence and coercivity collapse to zero; M(H) is reversible and Langevin-like.
implied_text: Thermal erasure of the directional latch on the observation window. Spatial-buffer twin of the thin-film mirror.
description: Too-small grains erase the latch on the observer's clock without reaching Tc.
value_text: KV ≲ 25 kT (~30 nm NdFeB lab window)
notes: Recording uses a 40–60 kT convention; Mössbauer windows sit near 10^{-8} s. Same contour, different clocks. T > Tc is the parent Curie collapse, not this volume cliff.

observed_text: Nd2Fe14B K1 ≈ 4.5 MJ/m³. Laboratory stability KV ≳ 25 kT gives V ≈ 2.3e-26 m³ (~30 nm linear) at 300 K. Magnetite blocking size is a 10–30 nm class for near-equant grains, not a single cliff.
implied_text: The latch hardware is unchanged from the parent magnet. Below the stability volume the barrier is under-provisioned by grain size, not by a missing anisotropy mechanism.
description: The spatial-buffer clause of the magnetic latch is a crystalline anisotropy cell at tens of nanometres for NdFeB at laboratory time.
value_text: V ≳ 2.3e-26 m³ (~30 nm NdFeB); KV ≳ 25 kT
notes: 25 kT is a timescale convention, not a single experimental cliff. Magnetite has no single portable diameter.

observed_text: The metal electrons must follow at the SPP frequency, below the screened plasma / interband edge — the same femtosecond class as reflection.
implied_text: Optical-cycle synchronization of the same free-electron gas. Drive above the screened edge unbinds the mode (ε_m+ε_d no longer negative).
description: SPR shares reflection’s femtosecond screening clock; the new constraint is momentum, not a new cycle time.
notes: Cross-cite reflection:clock_latency:plasma-period and plasma-frequency-cutoff for the numerical 0.3–1 fs band and for ω>ωp unbinding. This file does not restate those periods.

observed_text: A momentum-matching coupler is required. The coupler is a wavevector match, not a buffer, clock, barrier, lattice, field threshold, or thermal limit.
implied_text: The load-bearing k-match does not sit in the six allowed constraint tags. The thickness window is also not a single buffer number.
description: Tag-set gap plus a moving window: Medium mapping, not a contradiction of the electron-gas family.
value_text: k-match outside tag set; window ≠ floor
notes: File-level mapping remains Medium. Do not invent a seventh tag for one entry.

observed_text: A narrow dip appears in reflected intensity as angle or wavelength is scanned. The dip walks when the refractive index of the medium against the metal changes. Width tracks Im ε_m.
implied_text: A sharp angular or spectral absorption feature and a field bound to the interface, from synchronized oscillation of the metal electrons against the dielectric.
description: The stable output is the resonance dip and the interface-bound field, not a bulk mirror R.
notes: No universal R_min is quoted.

observed_text: None. Driven collective resonance, not a latch.
implied_text: No static barrier holds the dip. The mode exists only while it is driven.
description: SPR is a driven interface mode, not a stored directional state.

observed_text: The SPP wavevector lies outside the free-space (or dielectric) light line: k_sp > n_d ω/c. Light incident from free space on a flat metal surface does not produce the dip. Without a coupler (Kretschmann, Otto, or grating) there is no resonance, however good the metal.
implied_text: No in-plane momentum match → the interface mode is not launched → no dip.
description: Momentum match is load-bearing hardware and the primary collapse when the coupler or angle is absent.
value_text: no coupler, or θ / grating off the match
notes: total-internal-reflection supplies the prism evanescent field that Kretschmann and Otto use. Shared hardware, not a shared collapse.

observed_text: If the film is far from the working thickness window, or the metal is a poor, highly damped conductor, the feature washes out. Discontinuous morphology or a missing metal–dielectric face also kills the mode.
implied_text: Thickness off the window, islanded film, or no interface starves the bound-mode buffer.
description: Spatial failure is a window, not a one-sided 10 nm floor.
value_text: off the tens-of-nm / 40–50 nm Au window
notes: Do not treat 50 nm of gold as the SPR equivalent of reflection’s 5–10 nm cliff. Large γ washes the dip out rather than moving a sharp cliff.

observed_text: Field decay into the metal is of order the optical penetration depth (tens of nm). Decay into the dielectric is longer, typically a fraction of a visible wavelength up to about one wavelength. Propagating SPP in good Ag in the red can run tens of micrometres.
implied_text: The dielectric-side evanescent tail is an additional buffer. A coupler (prism index plus angle, or a grating period) is part of the hardware even though it is not the electron gas.
description: SPR occupies a wavelength-scale dielectric tail plus a metal-side optical skin.
value_text: dielectric tail ~λ/few to ~λ; metal decay tens of nm
notes: Metal-side decay is the optical skin owned by reflection / skin-effect. Propagation tens of μm is a run length, not the thickness window.

observed_text: Kretschmann film thickness sits in a window of tens of nanometres — commonly about 40–50 nm of Au in the visible — thick enough that a bound interface mode exists, thin enough that the prism field still reaches the outer metal–dielectric face. Continuous, not islanded.
implied_text: Three nested spatial resources: a metal–dielectric interface, a thickness inside the coupler window, and in-plane continuity. The window is not a universal 50 nm law.
description: SPR hardware is an interface plus a thickness window, not the 10–20 nm mirror floor.
notes: Geometric mean of 40–50 nm. Exact optimum is metal-, λ-, and coupler-dependent. Localized particle resonance (Au colloid ~520 nm) is a different spatial buffer and must not be averaged into this number.

observed_text: Carrier speed v is the long-wave acoustic slope. The transport clock is the scattering time τ = ℓ/v: boundary-limited and long at low T, umklapp-limited and short at high T. Zone-boundary / Debye periods remain the underlying oscillator clocks.
implied_text: Transport latency is ℓ/v, not the Debye period. No single τ is extracted.
description: The heat-current clock is the scattering time set by ℓ. Oscillator clocks stay with debye-cutoff.
notes: v owned by speed-of-sound; C(T) by debye-cutoff; this file owns ℓ.

observed_text: The mapping takes the kinetic formula and the Peierls umklapp distinction as descriptive data. It does not yet extract a particular ℓ(T) from node-level anharmonicity.
implied_text: The failing resource (ℓ) is identified; its value is not derived from node rules.
description: QSA names ℓ as the transport buffer but does not compute ℓ(T) from anharmonicity. Same unfinished anharmonicity as thermal-expansion.
value_text: κ = (1/3) C v ℓ taken; ℓ(T) underived
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Electronic thermal conductivity belongs with the electron population.

observed_text: Room-temperature class: diamond κ ∼ 10³ W m⁻¹ K⁻¹; typical oxide glasses κ ∼ 1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. A good crystal’s κ is small at the lowest T, rises, peaks (often tens of kelvin), and then falls.
implied_text: A material- and size-dependent κ(T) with the crystal peak-and-fall shape, produced by a synchronized phonon population limited by ℓ.
description: The transport machine emits a crystal κ(T) peak and a diamond-vs-glass class of about 10³ vs 1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.
value_text: diamond ~10³ W m⁻¹ K⁻¹; oxide glasses ~1; crystal peak-and-fall
notes: Kinetic structure κ = (1/3) C v ℓ is descriptive data; the 1/3 is a kinetic average, not a derived node rule.

observed_text: No latched barrier. Umklapp is a kinematic threshold in the phonon population (enough large-q modes occupied) rather than an activation barrier that stores a state. T → 0 starves C; T → T_m removes the grid.
implied_text: The transport spec has occupation and grid conditions, not a memory barrier.
description: Phonon heat current is not a latch. Umklapp is kinematic; T → 0 or melting starve the channel.
value_text: umklapp kinematic; C→0 as T→0; grid to T_m

observed_text: Specimen size below the intrinsic ℓ (Casimir) → κ set by L, not by bulk scattering. Low T, clean crystal: ℓ saturates at the specimen size, C ∝ T³, so κ ∝ T³.
implied_text: Spatial under-provisioning of the path makes the sample the buffer. That is a size failure of the bulk-κ spec.
description: When L < intrinsic ℓ, the heat current is boundary-limited and κ tracks the specimen, not bulk umklapp.
value_text: L ≲ ℓ (Casimir); κ ∝ T³ at low T
notes: Any one peak temperature or residual ℓ is sample-dependent (medium).

observed_text: This channel collapses if the grid is destroyed (melting) or if T → 0 (C → 0). It is not the electronic Wiedemann–Franz channel.
implied_text: Destroy the grid or starve C and this phonon κ is gone. Measuring a metal and attributing κ to phonons is the wrong machine.
description: Melting or T → 0 ends the phonon heat current. Electronic κ is a different population.
value_text: T → T_m or T → 0; not Wiedemann–Franz
notes: Cross-cite melting and electron-heat-capacity.

observed_text: Umklapp, defects, isotopes, or amorphization collapse ℓ and κ falls. At high T, C has saturated and ℓ continues to drop, so κ falls (often roughly as 1/T in simple crystals). Umklapp requires the reciprocal lattice; normal processes do not by themselves degrade a heat current in the Peierls accounting.
implied_text: ℓ is the load-bearing transport resource. Shorten it and the heat current dies even while the modes still exist.
description: The transport spec fails when the mean free path collapses — umklapp at high T, or defects / glass.
value_text: ℓ collapse (umklapp / defects / glass); κ often ~1/T at high T
notes: No reciprocal lattice, no umklapp (phonon-dispersion owns the zone). Same anharmonicity thermal-expansion names.

observed_text: A lattice that supports propagating acoustic modes, plus a mean free path. In the Casimir limit the spatial buffer is the specimen: ℓ saturates at the specimen size and shrinking L lowers κ at low T. In a glass the effective ℓ is already microscopic and the crystal-style peak never forms.
implied_text: Hardware is the phonon-carrying grid plus the scattering length ℓ. At low T the buffer is the sample itself.
description: Phonon κ requires a propagating lattice and an ℓ. Casimir makes the specimen the spatial buffer; a glass never provisions the crystal peak.
value_text: ℓ plus lattice; Casimir ℓ ~ L_sample
notes: A metal’s phonon channel is present but is not the macroscopic κ this entry maps.

observed_text: Equilibration clocks are medium-specific: collision time of order 10^{-10} s in standard air; phonon/electron exchange from picoseconds to nanoseconds in ordinary crystals. Radiative exchange is slower.
implied_text: Observation faster than the population’s exchange window returns a sequence of incomplete averages, not T.
description: The thermometer clock is the medium’s equilibration window; ordinary condensed samples have already finished on any mechanical or human clock.
notes: The numerical window is medium for any one sample and geometry. Do not treat 10^{-10} s as a universal machine clock.

observed_text: k = 1.380649e-23 J/K is defined in SI. The N^{-1/2} scatter is taken from ensemble formulae. No universal minimum N is measured.
implied_text: QSA takes the observed scatter and the measured equilibration time as buffer and clock. It does not derive k, or a minimum N, from node rules.
description: The statistical buffer is named as a class but not given a node-rule number. That is a gap, not a contradiction, and it recurs on every entry in this family.
value_text: k defined; no derived min N
notes: Treating the defined k as an extracted machine constant would over-claim.

observed_text: A body left in contact with a larger body, or isolated long enough, presents a single stable thermometer reading. Two bodies in contact converge; a third that matches the first matches the second.
implied_text: The stable product is one shared number T, and with it the conversion kT between that number and an energy scale.
description: T is the averaged output of the exchanging population, not a single-node property.
notes: k = 1.380649e-23 J/K is defined in SI, not an extracted machine constant. kT ≈ 4.14e-21 J at 300 K is arithmetic from that defined k.

observed_text: No latch holds T. Barriers elsewhere (Curie point, superconducting gap, melting) destroy or replace this average; they are not the resource that produces T.
implied_text: T is produced by exchange among contributors, not by a barrier that protects a written state.
description: Temperature has no energy barrier that stores a state.
value_text: no latch; exchange, not a barrier
notes: Negative latch spec. Melting, superconductivity, and permanent-magnet-latch own the replacements.

observed_text: A reading taken inside the exchange window, or on a subsystem that is not exchanging, is not the equilibrium T.
implied_text: Drive or observation faster than the averaging window is a clock failure of the family: the output is not T.
description: Observe inside the exchange window and the thermometer does not report T.

observed_text: With no exchange channel — no collisions, no radiation, no contact — two bodies do not converge to a shared reading.
implied_text: Zeroth-law contact is a resource. Isolation prevents a shared average.
description: Without an exchange channel the population cannot finish a common T.

observed_text: A sample with only a handful of independent contributors does not present a stable reading: successive observations scatter.
implied_text: Too few contributors → scatter dominates the mean → no stable thermometer reading.
description: Under-populated averages fail gradually; there is no single N at which T switches off.

observed_text: Relative energy (or inferred-T) fluctuations of a finite population scale as N^{-1/2}. There is no single universal N at which a thermometer starts working.
implied_text: The hardware is a large exchanging population. Required N is set by the stability of the reading against the instrument, not by a material constant.
description: Temperature requires a statistical buffer; collapse is gradual in 1/√N, not a connected-film or KV cliff.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Contrast with reflection’s 10–20 nm stack and the magnet latch cell.

observed_text: There is no separate expansion clock. The lattice clocks are the phonon spectrum; α(T) is the thermal occupation of those modes acting through γ. The laboratory length change follows the thermal equilibration time of the specimen, not an atomic period.
implied_text: α is an occupation readout of the existing phonon table, delayed only by specimen thermalization.
description: No dedicated expansion period is extracted. Laboratory ΔL follows thermal equilibration.
value_text: no separate clock; follows thermal equilibration
notes: Cross-cite phonon-dispersion and thermal-equilibrium-temperature.

observed_text: Anharmonicity is the stated condition and not a single hardware number. There is no measured γ_c at which expansion turns on. QSA does not derive the 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ class from node-well shapes.
implied_text: The resource (anharmonicity) is named; its strength is taken as data. Invar shows that α ≈ 0 can also be a cancellation, which must not be misread as γ = 0.
description: Expansion is located as the anharmonic correction, but that resource is not pinned to one measured hardware number the way ω_p or T_m is.
notes: File-level mapping is Medium. Quasi-harmonic ω(q) shifts organize data and do not supply a single how-anharmonic number.

observed_text: Metals as a class: α ∼ 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ near room temperature (handbook examples in that window: Al ∼ 2×10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, Fe ∼ 1×10⁻⁵ K⁻¹).
implied_text: A small, material-typical α(T) as the averaged length change of an anharmonic, thermally occupied grid.
description: The expansion machine emits a 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ metal class, not a universal α.
notes: value_si left null: class envelope, not one pin. A particular alloy’s α(T) is medium.

observed_text: No latched barrier and no single threshold number. The operating condition is γ ≠ 0 (anharmonic wells) plus a finite T. The stated collapse is the harmonic limit γ → 0, a condition on the wells rather than a measured T or E. There is no measured γ_c at which expansion turns on.
implied_text: Expansion is not a gated latch. γ of order one for many solids is a descriptive class, not a cliff.
description: No activation barrier and no γ_c. Anharmonic wells plus finite T are the operating condition.
value_text: γ of order one; no γ_c
notes: γ → 0 is the harmonic-limit statement. value_si is the order-one class, not a pin.

observed_text: A purely harmonic spring lattice would not expand — its mean bond length is independent of amplitude. γ → 0 (purely harmonic springs) → α = 0. This is the taxonomy collapse. It is a limiting condition, not a laboratory switch one flips on a given metal.
implied_text: Remove anharmonicity and the length-change machine disappears, even though moduli, sound speed, and the 3N mode count remain.
description: The harmonic lattice does not expand. That is the named collapse of this effect.
notes: Umklapp in thermal-conductivity-phonon draws on the same anharmonicity; the two entries should not assign contradictory γ.

observed_text: Invar (Fe–Ni near the 36 wt% Ni composition): α near zero around room temperature, not because the lattice has become harmonic, but because a magnetic / volume-magnetostriction channel cancels the ordinary anharmonic term.
implied_text: α ≈ 0 without harmonic wells. That is not the harmonic-limit collapse.
description: Invar’s near-zero α is a two-channel cancellation, not γ = 0.
notes: Cross-cite magnetostriction (volume channel). Composition 36 wt% Ni is in the file.

observed_text: α → 0 as T → 0, tracking the vanishing of the lattice heat capacity. High temperature: α continues until the grid fails (melting). There is no single α-defined collapse temperature analogous to T_m or T_C.
implied_text: Starve C_V and expansion stops even if γ is finite. Melting ends the solid’s α spec; it is not an α cliff.
description: Low T kills α with the heat capacity. Melting ends the solid; α itself has no T_C-style pin.
notes: Cross-cite debye-cutoff (C_V) and melting (high-T end of the same wells).

observed_text: A mechanically coupled lattice whose wells are not purely quadratic, large enough for a macroscopic length to be defined. If the restoring wells are purely quadratic, ⟨x⟩ is independent of T and α = 0. The harmonic grid that already produces speed-of-sound, elasticity, and debye-cutoff is not sufficient.
implied_text: Expansion is the anharmonic correction to the same ion-grid hardware. Harmonic springs provision moduli and a long-wave slope and still give α = 0.
description: The extra hardware is anharmonicity (γ ≠ 0), not a fourth reading of the harmonic springs.
value_text: γ ≠ 0 anharmonic wells; harmonic grid insufficient
notes: Invar adds a magnetic volume channel on top of the lattice term (magnetostriction).

observed_text: Clock is the optical period. TIR works across the transparency window of the two dielectrics.
implied_text: Clock is not the load-bearing collapse. The gate dies when n(ω) contrast disappears (X-ray δ→0, or an absorption band) — a failure of the underlying refraction machines.
description: TIR inherits the optical cycle of refraction; the collapse is geometric, not temporal.
notes: Cross-cite refraction-dielectric:clock_latency:optical-cycle (~2 fs visible) for the parent cycle time.

observed_text: The six allowed tags have no slot for angle or index contrast. spatial-buffer covers the interface, the evanescent tail, and frustrated-TIR starvation. It does not name the critical-angle gate.
implied_text: The sharp θc / n1>n2 collapse is recorded as a geometry/contrast gate but is not a first-class constraint tag.
description: Limitation of the tag list, not a reason to invent a tag for one file. Mapping still rates High because the collapses are sharp.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Not a new collective oscillator; kinematic gate on refraction’s n.

observed_text: Fresnel reflection coefficients have magnitude 1 (lossless media) for θ>θc, with an angle- and polarization-dependent phase.
implied_text: Unit reflectance for all θ>θc, together with a non-propagating field occupying a wavelength-scale volume on the far side.
description: The synchronized boundary response emits R=1 (lossless) and an evanescent occupancy, without a metal electron gas.
notes: Absorption in either medium → |r|<1 even above θc.

observed_text: Time-averaged Poynting flux through the interface is zero in lossless TIR. Energy still occupies the evanescent volume.
implied_text: Driven boundary response, not a latch. The word barrier for the low-index gap in frustrated TIR is a wave-tunneling metaphor, not an energy-barrier tag.
description: No stored state and no activation barrier. The gap is a spatial buffer.
value_text: no latch; evanescent gap is not ΔE

observed_text: θc = arcsin(n2/n1). Crown glass / air (n1≈1.50) θc≈41.8°; water / air (1.333) 48.6°; diamond / air (2.42) 24.4°. For θ<θc a propagating transmitted beam appears and R<1.
implied_text: Incidence below the geometric gate → the total-reflection output is gone.
description: The load-bearing geometric collapse is θ<θc.
notes: value_si is 41.8° in radians, textbook crown/air. Water 48.6°, diamond 24.4°. The cliff is θ<θc, not a universal angle. Metal reflection can give high R without any critical angle.

observed_text: A third medium placed inside the evanescent tail accepts a propagating wave. The isolation fails without any change in θ or in n1, n2.
implied_text: Spatial starvation of the 1/κ buffer by a third body destroys unit reflectance.
description: Frustrated TIR is buffer starvation of the evanescent volume.
notes: surface-plasmon-resonance uses this tail as a coupler rather than as a collapse.

observed_text: No real θc exists if n1≤n2.
implied_text: Without index contrast the geometry gate never opens.
description: n1≤n2 is a binary contrast collapse, sharper than refraction’s continuum.
notes: X-ray total external reflection is the same kinematic gate with inverted contrast (n_material=1−δ<1=n_vacuum).

observed_text: An evanescent field occupies the low-index side. Amplitude decay length 1/κ = λ0 / (2π √(n1² sin²θ − n2²)): of order λ/2π well above θc, several wavelengths as θ→θc+.
implied_text: An interface between two polarizable populations with n1>n2, plus a far-side buffer of order 1/κ. Same bound-charge machines as refraction-dielectric, not a new species.
description: TIR hardware is index contrast plus a wavelength-scale evanescent volume.
notes: Starve that gap with a third medium and the total-reflection output fails (frustrated TIR).

observed_text: Screening and core adjustment follow the parent-condensate electromagnetic / gap clocks (London / plasma scales; gap frequency). Flux-flow voltages, when present, sit on a much slower, geometry- and drive-dependent scale set by vortex velocity.
implied_text: This entry is not a voltage-standard clock; that lock lives on josephson-effect.
description: Mixed-state dynamics inherit the parent condensate clocks; flux flow is a slower, non-universal scale.
notes: Not the 483.6 MHz/μV lock.

observed_text: Pinning — the barrier that decides whether the mixed state is dissipationless — is set by microstructure (precipitates, grain boundaries, irradiation defects) and is not a universal function of λ and ξ.
implied_text: QSA does not yet have a clean buffer/barrier specification for that mesoscale step. The Hc1 / Hc2 / κ collapses do not depend on closing it.
description: Mixed-state classification is closed; the pinning landscape that protects R=0 is still underived, of the same kind as mesoscale coercivity.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Same class of gap as permanent-magnet-latch coercivity. Superconductivity records the R=0 side of this gap.

observed_text: Between Hc1 and Hc2 flux enters as a lattice of discrete tubes, each carrying one flux quantum Φ0 = h/2e = 2.0678e-15 Wb. The vortex lattice is seen by decoration, neutron diffraction, and STM.
implied_text: A mixed state whose field scale is set by ξ and λ, whose flux is packaged as an integer number of Φ0 tubes, and whose lattice spacing tracks √(Φ0/B), for as long as Hc1 < H < Hc2 and T < Tc.
description: The stable output is a field-tuned lattice of Φ0 phase defects.
notes: Same quantum as flux-quantization: a vortex is a phase defect that plays the role of the hole.

observed_text: Two field thresholds in type II, both temperature-dependent and both collapsing to zero at Tc: Hc1 (first flux entry) and Hc2 (gap destroyed; mixed state gone). Descriptive forms: μ0 Hc2 = Φ0/(2πξ²); μ0 Hc1 ≈ Φ0 lnκ / (4πλ²).
implied_text: Hc1 is the field threshold for first entry of a Φ0 defect. Hc2 is the field threshold that closes the gap. Pinning sites supply an additional barrier against vortex motion; that barrier protects the zero-resistance reading and is not the same threshold as Hc2.
description: The mixed-state window is the field interval between first vortex entry and gap closure.
notes: NbTi and Nb3Sn remain superconducting in tesla-scale fields at liquid-helium temperature; YBCO does so at liquid-nitrogen temperature, with a strongly anisotropic Hc2. Specific tesla numbers live on superconductivity.

observed_text: Above Hc2 the mixed state is gone and the sample is normal. T → Tc sends both Hc1 and Hc2 to zero.
implied_text: H > Hc2 destroys the ξ-buffer, closes the gap, and ends this artifact.
description: Upper-critical-field collapse is gap destruction, not first penetration.
notes: Collapse at Hc1 is a collapse of meissner, not of the gap. Treating them as one critical field would hide the vortex-lattice buffer.

observed_text: A moving vortex lattice produces a dissipative electric field. Zero-resistance transport in the mixed state therefore requires pinning. If the tubes can move, transport becomes dissipative even though the gap has not yet closed.
implied_text: Free vortex motion is a failure of the R=0 artifact while the gap and the lattice are still present. That is a different collapse from Hc2.
description: Unpinned flux flow dumps dissipation into the mixed state without closing the gap.
notes: Owned jointly with superconductivity, which owns R=0. Pinning landscape is the consistency-gap row.

observed_text: Type II when κ = λ/ξ > 1/√2. Type-I elements sit below this line and have a single thermodynamic Hc, typically tens of millitesla (lead is the high end of that class, μ0 Hc ~ 80 mT).
implied_text: Three nested spatial scales are required before this artifact exists as something other than a type-I Meissner state: ξ (core), λ (screening cloud), and the condition λ > ξ/√2.
description: Type II is the regime in which the screening cloud outruns the coherence-length core.
notes: λ is shared with meissner; ξ is the core size that closes at Hc2. This file owns the mixed-state window.

observed_text: Each vortex carries Φ0 = h/2e = 2.0678e-15 Wb. The areal density of vortices is B/Φ0; the lattice spacing is of order √(Φ0/B) (tens of nanometres at tesla-scale induction).
implied_text: Vortex lattice spacing is an extra, field-tuned buffer that has no type-I counterpart. The mixed state is a synchronized array of these defects, not a uniform condensate.
description: At tesla-scale B the mixed-state lattice is a tens-of-nanometres array of Φ0 tubes.
notes: value_si is √(Φ0/1 T) from the stated Φ0. Spacing tracks the field; it is not a material constant.

observed_text: Thermal attempt rates sit in the prefactor A T². Once over the barrier, vacuum transit is set by anode voltage and gap. Relative to any mechanical clock the emission, when it occurs, is already complete.
implied_text: Collection latency is not the gate. A T² is the attempt-rate prefactor, not a stored-state cycle.
description: Opening φ is not a laboratory-scale clock. Transit belongs to collection.
value_text: A T² attempt prefactor; transit is collection
notes: Theoretical A0 ≈ 1.20×10⁶ A m⁻² K⁻² is a current-density prefactor, not a period. No opening-time number is given.

observed_text: QSA takes φ as a measured surface specification. It does not here derive the 4.5 eV of tungsten from a more primitive node rule.
implied_text: No derivation of W’s 4.5 eV class from a surface-dipole plus chemical-potential construction. The collapse kT ≪ φ does not depend on closing that derivation.
description: The gate is located and shown to be a surface resource; its value is not derived from node rules.
notes: File-level mapping remains High; this clause is the underived step.

observed_text: Richardson–Dushman J = A T² exp(−φ/kT). Theoretical A0 ≈ 1.20×10⁶ A m⁻² K⁻². No optical illumination is required.
implied_text: Stable current density from a hot surface, with no optical drive, while surface, T, and collection field stay inside the envelope.
description: The machine’s stable product is a heat-opened surface current gated by φ.
notes: Apparent A of a technical surface is medium and is taken as a surface datum.

observed_text: Handbook polycrystalline φ: W ≈ 4.5 eV (often 4.54 eV); Cs ~2 eV; thoriated tungsten ≈ 2.6 eV. The same φ is the photoelectric threshold of the same surface.
implied_text: φ is the load-bearing gate. Heat opens it from below via the Boltzmann tail; a photon hν > φ opens the same gate from above. Schottky lowering modifies φ; it does not replace it.
description: Thermionic emission is the photoelectric-class surface gate opened by heat rather than by a photon. Not a latch; the electron leaves.
notes: value_si is clean W φ. Faces and contamination shift tenths of an eV. Cross-cite photoelectric-threshold.

observed_text: Emission is unmeasurable when kT ≪ φ. For clean W, φ/kT ~ 170 at 300 K (kT ≈ 26 meV) and ~20 at 2500 K. A tungsten filament at room temperature emits nothing measurable.
implied_text: Under-threshold thermal input is the non-occurrence of the conversion. That is the collapse of thermionic emission.
description: Below kT ~ φ the gate stays shut. A cold tungsten part is not a cathode.
notes: The Richardson tail is thermal occupation of states above a hard barrier, not a second channel.

observed_text: A measurable cathode current is the summed output of a large emitting area. Starving the area reduces current in proportion; it does not close the gate.
implied_text: Emitting area is a capacity, not a second spatial cliff.
description: Macroscopic J is a rate of independent escapes. Area scales the current, not the on/off of φ.
notes: No minimum emitting area is extracted. Space-charge / Child–Langmuir is a collection ceiling, not this capacity.

observed_text: The conversion event is single-electron: one occupied state at the surface, one barrier φ, one escape. There is no collective coherence volume analogous to the 10–20 nm mirror buffer.
implied_text: No collective buffer is required. One electron at a surface is the hardware. The gate lives in a surface atomic layer.
description: Negative spatial-buffer spec: the heat-opened gate is single-particle. Contrast with reflection’s 10–20 nm stack.
notes: Photoelectric twin of the same surface φ. How to query effects that do not need a spatial buffer.

observed_text: The absorption step itself tracks the X-ray cycle (~10⁻¹⁹ s at 10 keV). The observed edge width is set in part by the core-hole lifetime (femtosecond neighbourhood for many deep holes).
implied_text: Conversion latency is the X-ray cycle. Hole lifetime is a smear of the same gate, not a second threshold.
description: Inner-shell conversion finishes on the X-ray cycle; eV-scale edge width is a clock smear of Eb.
value_text: ~10⁻¹⁹ s at 10 keV; hole lifetime fs

observed_text: QSA takes Eb^(s) from tables. It does not here derive the 8.98 keV of copper’s K shell from a more primitive node rule.
implied_text: No derivation of the keV class from node rules. The collapse hν < Eb does not depend on that derivation.
description: The gate is located and tabulated; its value is not derived from node rules.
notes: File-level mapping remains High. Chemical shifts of a few eV on a 9 keV gate are a small environmental correction to the same barrier.

observed_text: At the Cu K-edge μ/ρ jumps from ≈38 cm² g⁻¹ to ≈278 cm² g⁻¹. The location of the jump is an elemental fingerprint.
implied_text: An element-specific step in μ(E) at Eb^(s), reproducible enough to identify the element and, with finer structure, its local chemistry.
description: The machine’s stable product is a named-shell attenuation jump.
value_text: Cu K step at 8.979 keV; μ/ρ 38 → 278 cm² g⁻¹
notes: XANES/EXAFS ride on the open channel; they do not create a second jump. The jump exists in atomic vapours.

observed_text: Cu K-edge at 8.9789 keV (~8.98 keV class); Cu L1 at 1.096 keV. Binding energies run from tens of eV (shallow cores) to tens of keV (deep K shells).
implied_text: Shell binding energies Eb^(K), Eb^(L), … are the operating gates — the same discrete energetic lock as φ and Eg, relocated to keV.
description: The X-ray absorption edge is a photoelectric-class inner-shell energy gate.
notes: value_si is Cu K (8.979 keV). Chemical shifts of a few eV relocate the same gate. Fluorescence and Auger are relaxation after the gate opens.

observed_text: Removing the element removes the edge. If the shell is already empty (highly ionized species) there is no jump.
implied_text: Missing hardware — no atom, or no occupied shell — closes that named gate.
description: The K-edge (or L-edge) is absent when the inner-shell node is not present.

observed_text: Below Eb^(s) that shell does not convert. At the Cu K-edge μ/ρ jumps from ≈38 cm² g⁻¹ to ≈278 cm² g⁻¹ only once the K channel opens.
implied_text: Under-threshold input is the non-occurrence of that shell’s conversion. That is the collapse of this edge.
description: Below the binding energy the named shell’s gate stays shut.
notes: Shallower shells and scattering may still attenuate the beam; they are other channels. Pair production at still higher energy is another family member, not this failure.

observed_text: The conversion event is one atom, one occupied inner shell. Thinning the sample reduces optical depth in proportion and does not close the atomic gate. Removing the element removes the edge.
implied_text: No collective coherence length analogous to optical reflection. One occupied inner shell is the hardware.
description: Negative spatial-buffer spec: the gate is single-particle.
notes: How to query effects that do not need a spatial buffer.
